ux.responsive_notes: The Releases view is a two-column layout on wide screens (left: current-release pipeline rail; right: history timeline). Below ~900px it stacks to a single column with the current-release rail first, so the live question ('is it green?') stays above the fold. Timeline rows collapse to sha + outcome chip on narrow screens, hiding duration/shipped-by behind the expand affordance. The Overview widget is width-agnostic (badge + one line + last-good), truncating the sha with a full value on hover/title. Rollback confirm and failure drill-in behave as a centered max-width (~520px) modal on desktop and a bottom sheet on <640px, both scrollable, with touch-targets ≥44px, focus management preserved across breakpoints, and a dismissible scrim that never traps attention when the pipeline is fine.

acceptance_criteria: When the current_version meets or exceeds a milestone's target_version and the milestone goal is marked complete, the pipeline creates a git tag matching the milestone name and posts release notes sourced from deploy history.
Release notes include all ticket IDs, titles, and the changelog entries produced during the version range from last shipped version to current.
If a tag for the milestone version already exists in the repository, the pipeline skips the release and logs a 'release already exists' activity entry rather than failing.
A Release chore ticket is created referencing the milestone, with all producing feature/bug ticket IDs as dependencies, and the milestone is marked as fulfilled.

tickets.title: Dependency Health Scanner
tickets.description: Third-party dependencies (Cargo.toml, package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod, etc.) are the single largest security and stability vector for any project, yet CoXAgent has no mechanism to scan for outdated or vulnerable packages. The team has no visibility into whether the codebase is shipping with已知 CVEs or stagnating on old major versions. This feature adds a periodic dependency scan that runs as part of the self-tuning loop: parse manifest files across all supported ecosystems, check versions against known registries, flag packages past their latest major version or with known high-severity CVEs, and auto-propose low-priority chore tickets for remediation — with a `depends_on` link to a master 'Dependency Audit' epic. It advances the product goal by giving the autonomous team full lifecycle ownership: not just building features, but maintaining the health of the entire codebase including its supply chain. Edge cases: some projects may lock a specific minor version for a reason (e.g. API compatibility); the scanner should not propose major-version upgrades without human review (auto-approve only for patch-level); private registry packages should be skipped if no credential is available; lock files (Cargo.lock, package-lock.json) should be the source of truth, not manifest files. Dependencies: builds on the existing `onboard.rs` manifest detection (already scans Cargo.toml, package.json, etc.), the `FileAuthService` port pattern for registry credentials, and the BA ticket creation pipeline. Risk: registry API calls introduce a network dependency in what is otherwise a deterministic loop — should cache results per cycle to avoid repeated lookups.
acceptance_criteria: The scanner parses lock files (Cargo.lock, package-lock.json, poetry.lock, etc.) from the project root and all subdirectories, extracting each dependency's current version.
Packages past their latest major/minor version (as reported by the registry) are flagged with a severity tier (patch: auto-approve, minor: warn, major: hold for human review).
CVE data is cross-referenced for flagged packages; any with a severity of 'high' or 'critical' triggers an immediate high-priority bug ticket regardless of version age.
Proposed dependency tickets include the current version, latest version, affected files, and a pre-linked `depends_on` to a master epic ticket, with the scan result attached as team context.

tickets.title: Debt sweep (cycle 10)
tickets.description: Scheduled tech-debt pass — no new features. Pick the highest-leverage debt and pay it down: reduce the lint/clippy baseline, delete dead code, fill missing module docs, strengthen the weakest test area.

technical.approach: CXA-C001 is ~80% already landed in main: `RunCycleUseCase::file_debt_sweep` (crates/application/src/use_cases/cycle/backlog.rs:129) already files one `Chore` titled `Debt sweep (cycle N)` on the leader's `cycle % 10 == 0` tick (crates/application/src/use_cases/cycle/mod.rs:519-521), deduplicates against any open sweep by title prefix across non-terminal statuses, embeds the current `DeployPort::lint` clippy count into the description when linting is supported, and the resulting Chore flows all the way through the normal pipeline because `selection.rs` includes `TicketType::Chore` in `design_candidates` (line 29), `ready_feature_candidates` (line 79) and `documentable_candidates` (line 64) — so SA makes it Ready, DEV-FEATURE claims it via the `ready_feature_candidates` import at run_dev/mod.rs:11, and DOCS documents it. Verified via `gitnexus impact file_debt_sweep --repo CoXAgent` -> risk LOW, 0 impacted symbols, contained to backlog.rs. So I am NOT redesigning the working core — I am completing the ticket by closing the two real gaps against house rules, as the smallest change: (1) zero test coverage exists (grep of cycle_tests.rs and backlog.rs shows no debt-sweep test), which violates 'features ship with tests'; (2) the cadence is bare `cycle % 10`, so I make the tick explicit and self-documenting. Plan: (a) extract the pure 'should file a sweep now, given an existing sweep is open and this is a sweep-th cycle' decision from the method body into a small pure predicate so it is directly unit-testable without an engine (matching the codebase's 'pure decision over snapshot, tested with a struct literal' pattern from hexagonal_gate/run_dev gates), then have `file_debt_sweep` call it; this keeps IO (store.load, deploy.lint, AddTicketUseCase) in the adapter method and the decision pure. (b) Add a unit-test module in backlog.rs covering: files exactly one Chore on a sweep-th cycle; does NOT file when a Pending/Ready/InProgress sweep already exists; does file again after the prior sweep reaches Done/Documented; carries the clippy lint note into the description when lint > 0 and omits it when None/0; the title carries the cycle number and the ticket's priority/complexity are Medium and has_ui=false. (c) Add a run_cycle integration assertion in cycle_tests.rs that cycle 10 lands a 'Debt sweep (cycle 10)' chore in state and that a non-sweep cycle (e.g. 1) does not. Architecture holds: everything stays in the application layer behind StateStorePort/DeployPort; no new ports, no IO in the pure predicate, dependencies still inward. No config change (the ticket explicitly says 'cycle 10' — cadence stays a constant, not a knob, per smallest-change).
technical.api_contract: No external API change. Internal: a new `pub(super) fn should_file_debt_sweep(state: &crate::state::ProjectState, cycle: u64) -> bool` (pure) in backlog.rs, factoring the current inline dedup+status-terminal check; `file_debt_sweep` keeps its signature `pub(super) async fn file_debt_sweep(&self, cycle: u64)` and its single call site at mod.rs:520 is unchanged. Reuses the existing `DeployPort::lint`, `AddTicketUseCase::new(...).execute(AddTicketInput{...})`, and `mutate_state` logging exactly as today — no port or contract changes.
technical.data_changes: None beyond the normal ticket creation the feature already performs: a new `Chore` ticket (`Debt sweep (cycle N)`) persisted via StateStorePort when no sweep is open on a sweep-th cycle, plus the existing `log_activity('SM', 'filed scheduled debt sweep', ...)` mutation. No schema/migration, no new state fields, no rollback concern. The filed ticket transits the standard lifecycle (Pending -> Ready via SA design -> Done via DEV -> Documented via DOCS) and terminates, so the dedup self-clears each cycle-10 window.
technical.test_plan: Run `cargo test -p coxagent-application` (and `cargo clippy --all-targets` per the CI fmt/clippy gates in crates/app/tests). New tests: (1) backlog.rs unit tests on the pure `should_file_debt_sweep` predicate using ProjectState struct literals: files=true on a sweep-th cycle with no open sweep; files=false on a non-sweep cycle; files=false when any Pending/Ready/InProgress sweep exists; files=true again once a prior sweep is Done/Documented/Rejected. (2) backlog.rs test on `file_debt_sweep` via a MemStore (pattern from cycle_tests.rs:13): a sweep-th call files exactly one Chore with title prefix 'Debt sweep', has_ui=false, Medium priority/complexity, and the expected acceptance_criteria; a second call with the sweep still open files nothing; description embeds the clippy baseline when a DeployPort stub returns Some(n>0), and omits it for None/0/absent deploy. (3) cycle_tests.rs integration: replace/drive `run_cycle(10)` on RoleAwareEngine and assert a 'Debt sweep (cycle 10)' Chore exists in state, and `run_cycle(1)` (or any non-sweep cycle) files none. Also re-run the existing full-cycle tests (one_cycle_carries_a_feature_from_proposal_to_done, deploys_*, rollback suite) to confirm no regression, and confirm the hexagonal_gate isn't tripped — the extracted predicate does no IO and stays in the application layer behind ports.
technical.alternatives: ALT-1 — Make cadence/configurable: add a `workflow.debt_sweep_every_n_cycles` config key. REJECTED: the ticket acceptance is fixed at cycle 10; adding a config key expands Config/WorkflowConfig surface and a serialization bump for a behaviour nobody asked to tune, violating smallest-change. ALT-2 — Hard-prioritize the sweep so it always outranks features: set priority High instead of Medium. REJECTED: a debt chore filed every 10 cycles at High would starve real feature/bug work and contradict the ticket's own 'no new features, pick the highest-leverage debt' framing; Medium already drains through readiness in priority order. ALT-3 — Have DEV execute the sweep inline in the same cycle it's filed (skip the ticket lifecycle). REJECTED: that bypasses the aggregate's guarded transition table, SA's design gate, and the acceptance/human review the whole team relies on, and would duplicate the existing file-a-chore + normal-pipeline flow — a larger, riskier change than what already works. The pure-predicate extraction (chosen) is the minimal change that makes the existing correct behaviour verifiable.

acceptance_criteria: The clippy/lint baseline is LOWER than before this ticket
No behavior change: full test suite still green

tickets.title: Cross-project knowledge reuse for agent briefs
tickets.description: PRODUCT GOAL LINE: makes the autonomous SDLC team deliver more reliably and cheaper. USER PROBLEM: an operator runs several projects on one hub, yet every agent brief (BA feature proposals, PD/SA design, Dev implementation, milestone planning) is grounded only in the current project's own wiki, docs, and closed tickets (knowledge_block/knowledge_brief in run_dev/briefing.rs and prompts.rs take a single project's state). The same problem gets re-solved — and re-paid for via metering — in every project, with no way to cite the prior art a sibling project already shipped. VALUE HYPOTHESIS: pooling an opt-in, searchable index of shipped designs, decisions, and durable doc pages across projects gives each run higher-quality offline context (fewer failure loops, lower cost_per_ship), and the operator stops buying the same solution N times. EDGE CASES: must not leak code/strategic content between projects (per-project opt-in scope, ACL on index visibility); irrelevant sibling matches must not bloat the context window/token cost (relevance threshold + hard size ceiling); sources must be named/cited so a cited design is traceable; staleness (prefer shipped/verified work; dedup against the current project's own pages). DEPENDENCIES: reuse the existing knowledge_block retrieval seam (wiki_block/prior_fix_block) behind a cross-project index; docs/ticket stores already exist per project, so the index can be derived from them. RISK/OPEN QUESTION: default on vs opt-in; how aggressive the relevance cut should be so cross-project recall never raises cost; whether the index is derived (scan shipped tickets/docs) or incrementally maintained.
acceptance_criteria: A per-project setting controls which sibling projects' content (docs pages, shipped designs, resolved bugs) may be cited in that project's briefs; off by default.

When enabled, an agent brief (verified for at least the Dev role and one design role) includes titles/IDs of matching sibling-project prior art with the source project and doc/ticket ID explicitly named.
Cross-project matches that score below a configured relevance threshold — or that exceed a hard token ceiling for the cross-project block — are omitted from the brief entirely.
A project's own wiki/docs/closed tickets still take precedence in retrieval, and no single-project's content is returned before the current project's own matches.
Adding cross-project citation never changes a brief when only a stale or low-relevance sibling match exists (empty-result case is a no-op, matching today's behavior).

tickets.title: Deploy history & one-click operator rollback
tickets.description: PRODUCT GOAL LINE: gives the human operator fast, audited control over a live deployment — the trust and recovery half of the autonomous delivery goal. USER PROBLEM: the cycle auto-rolls back on a health-gate failure, but after a merge the operator has no dashboard view of deploy/rollback history and no human-invoked way to revert the live app to a prior known-good version when a regression slips through post-merge. The only manual action today is 'deploy' from chat (chat.rs deploy_now), which cannot promote an older known-good. VALUE HYPOTHESIS: a visible deploy-history panel plus a confirmed one-click 'roll back to known-good' action lets the operator contain a bad release in seconds with a full audit trail, instead of editing or waiting for the next cycle. DISTINCT FROM CXA-F008 (automated build/publish release pipeline) and distinct from the autonomous in-cycle auto-rollback — this is an operator-invoked, post-merge control with history. EDGE CASES: no known-good deploys recorded (must not offer a no-op/broken rollback); the CONFIRM-for-expensive/undoable convention already used in chat must gate the action; rollback runs through the same mandatory post-deploy health gate as normal deploys; concurrent-deploy guard so a manual rollback cannot race an in-flight cycle deploy; every rollback recorded in the audit log with operator identity and before/after version. DEPENDENCIES: DeployRecord, DeployStatus, KnownGoodDeploy, and RollbackStatus already model the data in state/ops.rs; the manual-deploy seam in chat.rs shows the deploy-port wiring to extend. RISK/OPEN QUESTION: whether rollback should pause the cycle loop or just quarantine the current release; how far back history is retained for promotion.
acceptance_criteria: The dashboard shows a deploy/rollback history panel (version, ticket, timestamp, current health status) built from persisted DeployRecord/DeployStatus data.
When at least one prior known-good deploy exists, the operator can trigger a one-click rollback to it; the action is gated behind the existing confirm-for-undoable-action rule.
The rolled-back release is executed through the same mandatory post-deploy health gate as a normal deploy; the panel reflects success/failure and, on health failure, does not report a clean rollback.
With no recorded known-good deploy, the rollback control is disabled/unavailable rather than attempting a no-op or broken revert.
Every manual rollback writes an audit-log entry recording operator identity, the version rolled from and to, and the outcome, and the action is refused if a deploy/cycle is already in flight.

tickets.title: Incident post-mortem & prevention loop after rollback
tickets.description: GOAL LINE: the team must not only ship and revert safely, it must stop repeating the same class of breakage (safety/closed-loop pillar). USER PROBLEM: today auto-rollback (KnownGoodDeploy/RollbackStatus) restores the last-good build and the ops monitor files a generic 'app went down' bug, but nothing analyzes WHY the deploy passed gates then broke on the live health probe, so the same root cause keeps re-shipping and the team churns symptom tickets. VALUE HYPOTHESIS: operators and the DEV agent benefit when, after any rollback or deploy-failure, a blameless post-mortem is generated from the failing test/probe evidence plus the shipped diff, a structural root-cause prevention ticket is filed (deduplicated), and both are linked onto the DeployStatus/RollbackStatus — turning every incident into one 'why + fix-the-root' cycle instead of a revert-and-forget. EDGE CASES: (1) rollback skipped because migration_blocked or stale (no last-good within age window) — still write a post-mortem but mark it 'rolled-forward/stale', not 'rolled-back'; (2) same symptom already has an open root-cause ticket — link it, never duplicate; (3) one post-mortem per deploy revision, max one open per incident so the loop cannot storm the docs store; (4) an engine/auth outage (EngineIncident) does NOT trigger this path since it is infrastructure, not a shipped regression. DEPENDENCIES: existing DeployStatus/RollbackStatus state, docs store (DocStorePort), forge bug filing, #incidents chat channel. RISK/OPEN QUESTION: post-mortem quality depends on model; an LLM-free fallback (structural summary of test diffs + rollback reason) must be produced even if the model call fails. COMPLEXITY: medium. has_ui: true (view post-mortem from the deploy status on the dashboard).

technical.approach:
## Incident post-mortem & prevention loop after rollback — CXA-F012

### Goal & current behavior (evidence)
Today, when a forward deploy or its post-deploy test suite goes red, the leader tail (cycle/mod.rs:830-841) calls `RunCycleUseCase::attempt_rollback`, which redeploys the last known-good build in a dedicated worktree (ops.rs:160-252) and records outcome via `finish_rollback` (ops.rs:277-333) into `state.last_rollback` plus a `rollback_ok`/`rollback_failed` notification. The root cause is already filed as a deduped High bug by `file_deploy_bug`/`file_test_failure`. What is MISSING is any durable, inspection-grade *incident record*, any *prevention* so the exact bad commit cannot be re-inflicted, and any *team learning* from the rollback:
1. The rolled-back commit (`attempt_sha`) is never recorded as bad, so the self-healing retry (mod.rs:702-710 `was_in_rollback` -> redeploy every cycle) will re-deploy the SAME broken sha every cycle until a fix ships — the failure is replayed, not prevented.
2. No team lesson is recorded, so agents do not improve from the outage (contrast the dedicated lesson machinery `ProjectState::add_lesson` / `add_decision`, state/mod.rs:764-790).
3. No durable post-mortem history beyond the single `last_rollback` slot.

### Architecture (fits existing Clean/Hexagonal + DDD; dependencies point inward)
- **Domain/application**: pure decisions over the state snapshot — no new IO. All new logic goes in the existing `crates/application/src/use_cases/cycle/ops.rs` rollback use-case and a new value object in the deploy/outage bounded context `crates/application/src/state/ops.rs`. IO stays behind the existing `StateStorePort`/`GitPort`; nothing reaches for `std::fs`/`std::process` (hexagonal_gate preserved).
- **New domain value object** `IncidentRecord` (in `state/ops.rs`, the same file that already owns `RollbackStatus`/`KnownGoodDeploy` — the correct seam): `at`, `reason`, `failed_sha`, `to_sha`, `ok`, `summary`, `root_cause_ticket`, `lesson`. Persisted as a bounded rolling history `incidents: Vec<IncidentRecord>` (cap, e.g. last 12; `#[serde(default)]` so legacy state files load — matches `state_without_the_field_still_loads` in state/work.rs:265). Because `lite_state_value` (presentation/server/status.rs:58) serializes the whole `ProjectState`, the new field surfaces on the dashboard automatically with zero web-code change.
- **Prevention — bad-commit blacklist**: add `rolled_back_commits: BTreeSet<String>` (`#[serde(default)]`) recording every `to_sha`... wait — record the *failed* sha (`attempt_sha`), the commit that was rolled back as bad. In the leader deploy tail, before promoting a successful deploy to known-good, refuse `record_known_good` for a sha on the blacklist until its root-cause High bug is `Verified`. This is the prevention closure: a commit that once took the app down and needed a rollback is never re-promoted to `LAST_GOOD_REF` (ops.rs:118-139) until a fix has shipped and been verified — so the rollback cannot silently repeat.
- **Lesson loop**: on a successful rollback, derive a one-line lesson and feed it through the EXISTING `ProjectState::add_lesson` (deduped, capped, auto-fed to agent prompts) so the team learns team-wide without any new prompt plumbing.
- **Post-mortem step**: a new `post_mortem_after_rollback` method called from `finish_rollback`, which: records the `IncidentRecord`, blacklists the failed sha, and (on success) records the lesson. It resolves the already-filed root-cause ticket id by scanning open High bugs under the `Deploy failing`/`Tests failing` markers (no new plumbing; the same dedup the filers use).

### Non-functional
- **Partial failure**: all post-mortem writes are best-effort and idempotent (dedup on blacklist/history) inside existing `mutate_state`; a failed incidental write never rolls back the deploy outcome.
- **Data migration**: state gains two serde-defaulted fields; old state files load unchanged (serde default) — verified by an added compatibility test alongside state/work.rs:265.
- **Observability**: the existing `rollback_ok`/`rollback_failed`/`rollback_blocked` notifications are unchanged; post-mortem adds the activity + accident record visible on the dashboard.
- **Security**: no new authz surface — writes go through the same `System`-authored state mutations as the current rollback bookkeeping.

### Concrete plan
1. `crates/application/src/state/ops.rs`: add `pub struct IncidentRecord { at, reason, failed_sha, to_sha, ok, summary, root_cause_ticket: Option<String>, lesson: Option<String> }`.
2. `crates/application/src/state/mod.rs`: add `pub incidents: Vec<IncidentRecord>` and `pub rolled_back_commits: std::collections::BTreeSet<String>` (both `#[serde(default)]`, defaulted in the `Default` impl); add helper `add_incident(&mut self, rec)` (cap 12, dedup by failed_sha+at).
3. `crates/application/src/use_cases/cycle/ops.rs`: in `finish_rollback` (see the guarded-claim pattern elsewhere) append the incident + blacklist the failing sha; on rollback success derive + `add_lesson`; add private `root_cause_ticket_id(&self, state)` helper. Add a guard consult: in `record_known_good`, skip promotion when `state.rolled_back_commits` contains `sha` and its root-cause bug is not yet `Verified` (note in summary).
4. Tests in `crates/application/src/use_cases/cycle/cycle_tests.rs` (module already owns rollback tests): (a) a rollback records an IncidentRecord + blacklists the failed sha; (b) a blacklisted sha is not re-promoted to known-good until its bug is Verified; (c) a successful rollback records a team lesson; (d) blacklist/incidents survive a state round-trip and an old state file without the fields still loads.
technical.api_contract:
No HTTP API or message-schema change. `ProjectState` gains two serde-defaulted, backward-compatible fields that ride the existing `state_ep`/SSE serialization automatically:
- `incidents: IncidentRecord[]` (rolling history, capped ~12)
- `rolled_back_commits: string[]` (set of failed-commit shas blacklisted from known-good promotion)
`IncidentRecord` shape: { at: string, reason: string, failed_sha: string, to_sha: string, ok: bool, summary: string, root_cause_ticket?: string, lesson?: string }. Internal seams: new `RunCycleUseCase::post_mortem_after_rollback` called from `finish_rollback`; `record_known_good` gains a blacklist-guard consult. No port signatures change (StateStorePort/GitPort untouched).
technical.data_changes: Forward-compatible and reversible. Add `IncidentRecord` struct in `state/ops.rs` and two fields on `ProjectState`: `incidents: Vec<IncidentRecord>` and `rolled_back_commits: BTreeSet<String>`, both `#[serde(default)]` with values in the `Default` impl. Existing persisted state files load unchanged (serde default fills the new fields); the rollback requires no rewrite. Rollback of this feature = stop writing the fields; `last_rollback` (the existing single-slot record) remains authoritative if we ever need to drop the richer incident. Blacklist pinning is consult-only against state — no git ref mutation required.
technical.test_plan:
Extend the existing rollback test module `crates/application/src/use_cases/cycle/cycle_tests.rs` (already the home of `rollback_failure_stops_after_one_retry_and_escalates` etc.) with pure-state, no-IO tests using the existing `MemStore`/double fakes:
1. `a_rollback_records_an_incident_and_blacklists_the_failed_sha` — after `run_cycle`, state.incidents has one record linking failed_sha/to_sha/reason/root_cause_ticket, and the failed sha is in rolled_back_commits.
2. `a_blacklisted_sha_is_not_re_promoted_to_known_good_until_its_bug_is_verified` — with the bad sha still Open, a later successful deploy of that sha must NOT move `last_good_deploy`/`LAST_GOOD_REF`; after the High bug is `Verified`, promotion resumes.
3. `a_successful_rollback_records_a_team_lesson` — state.lessons grows by exactly the derived lesson (deduped).
4. `incidents_and_blacklist_survive_state_round_trip` + legacy-load guard — extend/add alongside `state_without_the_field_still_loads` (state/work.rs:265) asserting an old serialized state without the new fields still deserializes. Run `cargo test -p coxagent_application use_cases::cycle` plus the gate tests `cargo test -p coxagent_app --test hexagonal_gate` (no new direct-IO application file introduced). No web/playwright change, so `cd e2e && npx playwright test` is unaffected.
technical.alternatives: 1) A brand-new `Incident` aggregate + dedicated ticket type in `crates/domain`. REJECTED: it adds a domain enum/transition surface for a phenomenon the existing High bug already captures; over-engineered. The incident is a durable *record* of the rollback, not a new piece of scheduled work — the ticket system already schedules both the root-cause fix and its regression. 2) Mail/chat only — emit a post-mortem message into #agents and stop. REJECTED: chat is volatile and not queryable; it satisfies neither prevention (blacklist) nor durable dashboard history, and the team's own lessons show rejected-on-approach closures hinge on a checkable artifact, not a message. 3) Enforce prevention purely at the git layer with a tracked 'bad-refs' file in the repo. REJECTED: it needs new GitPort IO + a new adapter and violates the IO-through-a-port discipline for what is a pure state decision; the blacklist belongs in the same state store as the deploy records, where `mutate_state` already guards atomicity.

ux.user_flow: When a deploy or its post-deploy tests fail, the system auto-rolls back to the last known-good build (one retry, then escalates). The operator lands on the dashboard's new 'Incidents' tab and sees the rollback promoted from a buried status to a titled incident card: WHEN it happened, WHAT shipped (commit sha), the health-check evidence that fired it (HTTP status + response time; raw code never shown alone), and what state the app is now in (rolled back and healthy / rollback skipped / rollback itself failed and service may be down). CTA stack, in order: 'See the bug' (jumps to the root-cause bug ticket the system filed), 'Follow the fix' (links the bug's working branch), and 'Saved as a lesson' (shows the distilled prevention line). The operator reviews for a mis-categorization, corrects severity, and confirms. The loop then closes automatically: root cause works the backlog as a High bug; at sprint retro the SM distills the incident into one concrete lesson that lands in the ('Lessons' panel) and feeds the next ticket's briefing so the same failure is prevented, and a related-ticket chip links any previously-closed ticket with the same symptom so the operator sees 'we've seen this before'.
screens: Dashboard (home) — Deploy status header: green 'Shipped & healthy' / red 'Incident — rolled back' / amber 'Rollback skipped' banner, one line, with an 'Open incidents' shortcut; durable link to the Incidents tab

Incidents tab — the post-mortem list: each incident is a card with timeline (failed forward deploy → rollback → current state), evidence accordion (health-check probe detail), linked root-cause bug ticket, and prevention status; empty state ('No open incidents. Every deploy is current job: keep the health gate green.')

Incident detail (opens inline or as a drawer) — full timeline, deploy summary + commit sha, health-check evidence, rollback outcome or the skip reason with its exact human-readable explanation, linked bug ticket with severity, and the prevention/lesson field

Lesson panel (shared 'Lessons' side panel already used for team memory) — the distilled single-sentence prevention, age-stamped, deduped, capped at 12; each entry ties back to the incident that produced it
Related-ticket surface — on the incident card/bug ticket, a 'Seen before?' chip linking the most recent closed ticket with the same symptom so the operator can read the last resolution
Notification stream entry — the rollback event posts to the team channel (already happens server-side) with the same card's title so in-app and channel agree
component_states: Incident card — neutral/loading (skeleton, 'Resolving…'); success/green (app rolled back and healthy, 'Back up on <sha>'); warning/amber (rollback skipped — stale known-good or migration in the way — 'No automatic rollback; service may be degraded'); error/red (rollback itself failed — 'Service may be down — a High bug is filed'; empty (no incidents — 'All clear'); disabled (CTAs greyed out until the root-cause bug is filed)
Timeline step — per-entry state: done (filled check), in-flight (spinner + 'Running'), failed (error), skipped (muted with reason)

Health-check evidence reveal — collapsed 'See probe detail' (HTTP status + response time), expanded table, error state 'No probe recorded' when a rollback path discarded detail (the known COX-F005 gap)

Root-cause bug chip — open (linkable, 'Open'), filed-but-pending (disabled 'Filing…'), deduped (links the existing bug instead of a new one, 'Already tracked'), none/succeeded-recovered ('Nothing to fix')

Lesson field — empty (placeholder 'Not yet distilled — due at next retro'), pending (amber 'Scheduled for retro'), saved (green teal check, deduped: 'Already captured'), stale (muted 'Replaced by a newer lesson')
Close-incident action — enabled for a human approver only (RBAC), confirming text 'Mark resolved & archive'; disabled for viewers with a tooltip 'View-only'
Incident list filters — toggle 'Open / All', active-state highlight, and an empty-results error state
ux.responsive_notes: Single-column card stack on a mobile/narrow viewport with the timeline folding to a compact left rail and the evidence accordion collapsing by default; two-column list+detail on ≥1024px so a selected incident's detail sits beside the list without navigation. Interactive color is never the sole signal: every state carries an icon plus a text label (red/green/amber is reinforced, never replaced, by words) to satisfy WCAG contrast (≥4.5:1 text, ≥3:1 large/graphical) and color-blind safety; all CTAs and reveals are keyboard-reachable (tab order, Enter to expand, focus visible), each card has an aria-label summarising status, and severity is never shown as a raw error code — it maps to one of: healthy, rolled back, rollback skipped, rollback failed. The SPA dashboard honours the hub's assigned host port (never port 4000) and any UI change must pass the e2e Playwright golden-screenshot + console-error gate.

acceptance_criteria: After every rollback (RollbackStatus.ok=true) or deploy_failed followed by auto-rollback, the cycle produces a post-mortem document written to the docs store and posted to the #incidents channel, linked back from the DeployStatus/RollbackStatus.

The post-mortem records root cause from the failing health/test evidence + the shipped diff and files a root-cause prevention ticket; if an open ticket with the same symptom already exists it is linked and NOT duplicated.
Rollback skipped for migration_blocked or stale produces a post-mortem explicitly marked 'rolled-forward/stale' rather than 'rolled-back', and still files the prevention ticket.
Engine/auth infrastructure incidents (EngineIncident) do NOT trigger a post-mortem; and no more than one post-mortem is ever open per deploy revision or incident.
If the post-mortem model call fails, a deterministic structural summary (rollback reason + test/diff evidence) is still written — the feature never hangs the cycle.

tickets.title: Budget forecast & cost attribution (predictive FinOps)
tickets.description: GOAL LINE: FinOps / cost safety pillar — the loop already meters spend per role/operator and hard-stops at caps, but only reactively once the cap is hit (approaching_cap / budget_warning). USER PROBLEM: an operator cannot see whether today's burn rate will trip the daily or lifetime budget NEXT week, or which role/ticket is driving it, so they either pause too early or get surprised at the cap. VALUE HYPOTHESIS: operators gain a forecast (projected budget-exhaustion date + confidence from the existing per-day spend history in metrics.rs compute/DayCount) and attribution (top cost drivers by role and by ticket) surfaced in the Cost view and, when the projected hit is N days away, as an early chat/webhook warning — a proactive knob where today there is only a reactive brick wall. EDGE CASES: (1) no spend history yet -> render 'no forecast yet', never crash; (2) budget_usd absent/cap non-positive -> forecast shown as 'no cap' (matching approaching_cap behavior) rather than a false date; (3) daily cap and lifetime cap forecast separately and the earliest one wins; (4) predictive warning is a NEW event kind (e.g. budget_forecast) so existing ChatNotifier/WebhookNotifier forward-compatibility rules apply. DEPENDENCIES: existing metrics/AgentEvals/DayCount computation, FinOps metering state, Cost dashboard view, notify port. RISK/OPEN QUESTION: forecast accuracy on sparse history — the confidence band must widen, not fabricate a date, when fewer than N days of data exist. COMPLEXITY: medium. has_ui: true.
acceptance_criteria: The Cost view shows a projected budget-exhaustion date (with a confidence band) computed from the existing per-day spend history, and separately for the daily and lifetime caps with the earliest taken when both are set.
Spend drivers are attributed: the top cost role and top cost ticket (by metered spend) are shown for a configurable window.
With no spend history, the view shows 'no forecast yet' and never fails; with no cap set it shows 'no cap' and never dates zero infinity.

A predictive warning event (budget_forecast) is emitted when the projected hit is within the configured horizon, delivered through the existing chat and webhook notifier sinks, and is distinct from the reactive at-cap budget_warning.

tickets.title: Cross-project API contract-drift detection & impact alerting
tickets.description: GOAL LINE: multi-project hub / distributed-safety pillar — the product runs an autonomous fleet of projects behind one hub, and each project owns its services; nothing today watches for one project changing a shared API and silently breaking consumers in another project. USER PROBLEM: when an autonomous project changes or removes a route or response field its own tests pass in isolation, but a consumer project in the same hub that fetches that endpoint breaks hours later with no signal about the source — and the existing code-graph (CodeGraph::dependents/callers) and the group contract registry are per-workspace and unused cross-project. VALUE HYPOTHESIS: hub operators benefit when a change in a provider project is diffed against the pinned expectations of consumer projects; a breaking change (removed/renamed field, removed/changed route) emits a notification and files a follow-up ticket in the consuming project BEFORE its next cycle silently fails. EDGE CASES: (1) a consumer with no indexed contract/expectation is skipped with a note, not flagged (no false positives); (2) additive-only changes (new field/route) are tolerated, never alerted; (3) a truly breaking change against a pinned expectation is the only alert class; (4) no provider contract, or provider not indexed, is reported as 'cannot assess', not silence or alarm. DEPENDENCIES: existing code-graph per project, the group contract-registry extraction (group_sync/contracts.json), hub registry of projects, notify port + file-bug. RISK/OPEN QUESTION: requires provider projects to actually expose contracts AND consumers to be contract-indexed; a generic 'generally useful' version without stable cross-index symbols would fail the goal gate — scope is a working proof on the hub's indexed projects, in the consuming project's next cycle. COMPLEXITY: large. has_ui: false.
acceptance_criteria: When a provider project's API changes a response field or route that a consumer project in the hub pins as an expectation, a breaking-change cross-project alert is emitted (notify) and a follow-up ticket is filed in the consuming project.
Additive-only API changes (new field, new route) never produce an alert or ticket.
A consumer with no indexed contract/expectation is recorded as 'not assessable' rather than flagged as broken.
A provider with no extractable contract or that is not indexed is reported as 'cannot assess', never as clean and never as broken.
The detection runs on the shared hub registry and re-uses the existing group contract registry, with the outcome surfaced alongside the consuming project's next cycle.

tickets.title: Cross-project knowledge: sibling-project index and discovery port (from CXA-F010)
tickets.description: Foundation for CXA-F010. Today the only cross-project knowledge is one flat hub-wide `hub_lessons.md` (a write-only bullet list capped at 30, injected into every DEV prompt via `hub_lessons_block` and mirrored daily into each project's wiki in `ceremonies.rs:394`). There is no notion on the hub of 'which other projects exist and where they live', so a brief cannot reuse a sibling project's wiki (`state.docs`), closed tickets, repo docs, or team memory. This sub-ticket adds the plumbing to enumerate sibling projects on the hub behind a port — an outbound `HubProjectsPort` (adapter in `crates/infrastructure`, decision-layer API in application) that returns each sibling's id, working-tree path, and doc/wiki/lesson root. The adapter reads the hub project registry (`run_hub`/`ProjectHandle` in `crates/app/src/lib.rs` and `builders.rs`, which already knows sibling projects for host-port allocation) and exposes a pure `SiblingProjects` value the briefing layer can consume. This is pure capture/discovery with zero prompt-surface change, so it is independent and shippable alone.
acceptance_criteria: A new outbound port (`HubProjectsPort`) enumerates sibling projects on the hub: id, working-tree path, and per-project wiki/docs/lessons root; the adapter is wired in `builders.rs` next to where sibling host ports are already computed.

All IO (reading the registry, resolving paths) lives in an infrastructure adapter behind the port; the application layer contains only a pure function over the returned `SiblingProjects` value — `crates/app/tests/hexagonal_gate.rs` stays green with no new grandfather entries.
The port returns `None`/empty (not an error) when the hub has no other projects or the registry is absent, so current single-project behavior is byte-identical.
The sibling enumeration is unit-tested with an in-memory double: zero siblings, one sibling, and many siblings each yield the correct, sorted, de-duplicated list.
Adding the port and adapter does not change the task prompt (`run_dev/briefing.rs` `build_request`) or the `hub_lessons_block` output in any way — proof it is an independent additive layer.

tickets.title: Cross-project knowledge reuse in agent briefs: sibling retrieval blocks (from CXA-F010)
tickets.description: The behavioral core of CXA-F010, built on the sibling-project index. Extend the agent brief so a DEV/SA (and BA/PO/PD via the same primitives) working ticket T can see the RELEVANT knowledge a sibling project already wrote down about the same subject. Extend the `knowledge_brief` path in `run_dev/briefing.rs` to consult the `HubProjectsPort` and, for each sibling, reuse the existing match-and-cap primitives already used intra-project — `wiki_block`, `prior_fix_block`, `repo_docs_block`, `team_memory_block_relevant` — scoped to the sibling's wiki/tickets/docs, with `exclude` dropping any project with no system-match so noise stays out of the brief. Output is a new prompt block (e.g. `## Knowledge from {sibling} projects`) appended only when a sibling match clears a relevance floor, capped in total characters so the brief stays prompt-sized. Keep `prompts.rs` small: extract the new cross-project assembly into its own documented file/use-case (`run_dev/sibling_brief.rs`) and move `hub_lessons_block`'s feed through the same, leaving the file smaller than found. Include an `ASK SA`-style border so an agent never mistakes sibling context for this project's rules.
acceptance_criteria: A sibling whose wiki/closed-tickets/docs/team-memory share distinctive terms with a ticket's title+description+design gets a bounded, relevance-ranked block in the task prompt; a sibling with no match contributes nothing (empty block, no placeholder).
The sibling block is character-capped (brief stays prompt-sized) and the number of sibling projects/entries is capped, matching how intra-project blocks are bounded today.
The sibling context is clearly labelled with the source project id so the agent treats it as context, never as this project's law; a one-line rule in the block states the project-boundary discipline.

Run through the port with an in-memory double: a sibling wiki/document match produces the block, a no-match sibling produces none, and a hub with zero siblings changes the current brief by not a single byte (equivalence with today's output).
New unit tests cover retrieval ordering, the relevance floor, the char cap, and the 'it already lives in this project' dedupe; `crates/app/tests/hexagonal_gate.rs` and the prompts gate remain green.

tickets.title: Cross-project knowledge reuse: hub knowledge dashboard & curation (from CXA-F010)
tickets.description: Make the cross-project knowledge discoverABLE and curatable (the presentation side of CXA-F010, and the pattern the repo already enforces: knowledge must be readable where people read, cf. the daily mirror of hub lessons into each wiki in `ceremonies.rs`). Add a small hub-level view listing every project's shared/sharable knowledge — the sibling index from sub-ticket 1 plus the hub-wide lessons — so an operator can see at a glance what one project is teaching the rest and what a sibling shares that this one does not, and can unpublish/reclassify an entry. Render the sibling-relevant knowledge that sub-ticket 2 computes (expose the same shared function, not a re-implementation). Use the existing thin-presentation rule: the dashboard route/component only calls a use-case; decisions (which entries are shared, relevance, caps) stay in application functions so they are unit-testable without the UI. Ship the dashboard change against the existing classic-script web UI (`web/js/*.js`, `web/app.css`, ONE shared scope, load order matters) and must pass `cd e2e && npx playwright test`.
acceptance_criteria: A hub-level knowledge view lists each sibling project's sharable knowledge (wiki, closed tickets, docs, lessons) from the same data/function the agent briefs use — no second implementation of matching or extraction.
An operator can mark a shared entry as hidden/unshared for this brief surface; the change is persisted and reflected in the very next generated brief block.
The view surfaces an empty/off state when the hub has zero sibling projects or nothing shared, without erroring.

The UI ships via the existing classic-script web stack (no new framework), respects the one-shared-scope/load-order rule, and `cd e2e && npx playwright test` passes (golden screenshots + console-error gate).
Matching/extraction logic is covered by application-level unit tests independent of the UI; a non-existent/deleted sibling project renders as skipped, not error.

tickets.title: Agent Cycle Performance Dashboard — velocity, burn rate, and pattern recognition
tickets.description:
The cycle loop already collects CycleMetrics, Tuning, spend data, ticket_fail_attempts, and pr_rescue_attempts across every phase — but these values are persisted and never surfaced in a structured, trend-aware way. Operators and the PO can query individual counters (the Cost view shows spend) but there is no unified health overlay that tells them whether agents are improving, stalling, or regressing over time.

User problem: The PO/SM has no evidence-based way to answer 'are we moving faster or slower?' or 'which ticket type causes most failures?' without manually reading through transcripts and cost logs. Sprint velocity exists as a historical record but is not correlated with cost burn, agent role performance, or failure mode frequency.

Value hypothesis: The PO and SM can assess team health at a glance. The PO uses trend data to make better prioritisation decisions (e.g. deprioritising high-cost-low-signal ticket types). The SM identifies patterns (e.g. 'BA proposals with complexity=large fail 73% of the time') and adjusts grooming or scoping standards.

Product goal alignment: 'Self-tuning: the loop reads its own evals daily' (README) and 'cost-approval gate for expensive tickets' — this turns those signals into structured insight rather than raw data buried in state.

Dependencies: Existing CycleMetrics and Tuning structs in application/src/metrics.rs; spend data in ProjectState; ticket lifecycle data in all cycle phase use cases.
Risk: The BA must surface data only — never make autonomous decisions. A separate guard on the metrics endpoint could prevent any agent from using these charts as input to cycle decisions.

technical.approach:
Architecture decisions:

**Layering:** Pure domain core -> application metrics computation -> infrastructure adapters -> presentation API/Web. Dependencies point INWARD.

**Module boundaries:**
- Application: crates/application/src/metrics/cycle_perf.rs (new file for analytics)
- Presentation API: New endpoint in crates/presentation/src/server/status.rs
- Web: New JS module crates/presentation/src/web/js/performance.js + index.html

**Key patterns:**
- Compute-from-state: metrics derived from ProjectState (tickets, sprints, spend, activity) — pure functions like existing metrics.rs pattern
- Hexagonal port: StateStorePort for reads

**Non-functionals:**
- Security: Same auth as /metrics endpoint — project member via middleware
- Failure modes: Graceful fallback via serde defaults
- Migration: No data migration — reads existing ProjectState fields

**Concrete plan:**
1. Define CyclePerfData types (velocity, burn_rate, patterns)
2. Implement compute_cycle_perf(state) — pure function
3. Add GET /api/projects/:pid/cycle-perf endpoint
4. Build performance view (velocity chart, burn rate, pattern cards)
5. Write tests for metrics + endpoint + e2e
technical.api_contract:
GET /api/projects/:pid/cycle-perf

Query: ?limit=30&window=w1,w2,w4 (cycles to include, aggregation periods)

Response 200: {
  velocity_by_sprint: [{sprint: 1, committed: 8, done: 6, at: "2026-08-01"}],
  burn_rate: [{day: "2026-08-01", tickets: 12, cost_usd: 45.50, total_remaining: 44.50}],
  per_sprint: {shipped, avg_sprint_duration, completion_rate},
  quality_by_sprint: [{sprint: 1, failed_deploy_pct, test_failure_rate, pr_rework_rate}],
  pattern_summary: {most_failed_gates: [{name: "clippy", count: 5}], failure_layer_dist: {spec: 10, gate: 55, design: 25}, recurring_tickets: [{id: "CXA-B001", fail_count: 3}]},
  cycle_counts: {ba, sa, pd, dev, test, docs},
  cost_per_cycle: [{cycle: 1, cost_usd: 0.45, by_role: {dev: 0.20, sa: 0.15, test: 0.10}}],
  deploy_success_rate_7d: 0.92
}

Error 404/500 as per existing pattern
technical.data_changes:
No new persisted data — all derived from ProjectState:
- tickets[].(status, type, priority, complexity) for velocity
- sprint[].committed + sprints[] for velocity history
- spend.(total_cost_usd, by_role, runs_by_role) for costs
- history[] for deploy metrics
- activity[] for cycle timing
- ticket_failures[] for pattern recognition
No schema_version bump required
technical.test_plan:
Application layer tests (cycle_perf_tests.rs):
- velocity computes from sprint records (committed vs done)
- burn rate tracks cost per day with cap projection
- quality metrics aggregate per-sprint (deploys, PR rework, failures)
- pattern recognition identifies most-failed gates
- empty state handled gracefully (all defaults)

Endpoint tests:
- GET /api/projects/:pid/cycle-perf returns 200 for valid project
- Returns 404 for missing project
- Auth gating via existing middleware

E2E tests (playwright under e2e/):
- Performance view loads from dashboard nav
- Clicks through views, renders charts
- Verify golden screenshot baseline
technical.alternatives:
1. Store cycle metrics in separate file — rejected because it duplicates ProjectState and creates dual-write risk; compute-from-state keeps one source of truth
2. Add analytics as separate domain types — rejected because metrics are derived views, not business entities; keeping in application layer avoids polluting domain
3. Microservice split for analytics — rejected because it's the same database, same deploy, shared state; would add network overhead for intra-process calls

ux.user_flow: The SM/Lead opens CXA-F018 to triage cycle health. They land on the Overview tab first and scan one glance: 7-day velocity (tickets shipped per cycle), burn rate ($/cycle over last 10 cycles), and an anomaly flag if churn or cost spiked. If velocity is declining, they drill into the Trend tab and see cycle-by-cycle velocity bars with a 3-cycle moving average; if burn rate is too high they switch to the Rate tab and see cumulative spend, daily spend rate, per-agent spend share, and cost-per-ticket with a budget runway estimate. If anything looks odd, they open the Patterns tab to see per-agent cycle-time box-plot style bars, error-type distribution, and a top-3 patterns callout generated deterministically from state (e.g., 'dev_feature retry rate increased 40% in last 10 cycles'). From any KPI they can click through to the ticket-level data behind it. The entire dashboard is read-only; action buttons (adjust budget, pause cycle) are in the existing settings page. All charts render server-side as SVG to avoid JS dependencies — same pattern as the existing burndown chart. No data leaves the frontend after the initial load.
screens: view-performance (id='view-performance', parent nav link under Workspace: 'Performance')
Sub-section A: Overview (default) — hero strip of 6 KPIs for the current sprint window
Sub-section B: Trend — cycle-by-cycle velocity + moving-average line on same chart
Sub-section C: Burn Rate — cumulative spend area chart + daily burn rate KPIs + budget runway warning
Sub-section D: Patterns — per-agent cycle time distribution, error-type pie, top patterns
Modal overlay: Cycle Detail — single cycle drill-down showing each agent's phase timings, output, and errors
component_states: KPI card (kpi.css): loading (spinner skeleton), error (red border + 'Refresh' CTA), normal (value + label), warning (amber border for KPIs outside ±1σ), critical (red border for budget overrun)
Velocity bar chart: default (bar per cycle height-scaled), hover (tooltip with cycle #, tickets, $), active/slice selected (highlight), empty state ('No cycles shipped yet')
Cumulative spend chart: same states; when spend=0 shows dim placeholder 'No spend data' instead of bars
Sprint progress ring: indeterminate (spinning arc) while sprint compute is running, complete (ring fills to 100%), overdue (ring turns amber with 'OVERDUE' label)

Patterns card: loading skeleton, populated (top pattern highlight + detail list), none-detected (dim text 'No significant patterns in last 15 cycles)', error ('Unable to compute patterns — insufficient data')
Cycle Detail modal: closed (not shown), loading (skeleton), populated (agent timing table + output summary + errors), empty (cycle had no work — same empty state text)

KPI color coding: green (within ±1σ of rolling mean), amber (1-2σ outlier), red (>2σ OR budget breached). Consistent across all tabs. Churn red if >2.0, amber if >1.5 per existing agent-evals conventions.
ux.responsive_notes: Desktop (>1024px): all 4 sub-sections in 2-column grid (row2), charts side-by-side with data tables. Tablet (600-1024px): stacks to single column, charts take full width, KPI grid compresses to 2 columns instead of 3. Mobile (<600px): single column, KPIs stack to 1-col, hide moving average line on velocity chart (show only bars with tap-to-show), Patterns tab collapses to top-1 pattern only, Cycle Detail modal becomes full-screen slide-up instead of centered overlay. All touch targets ≥44px. Charts use SVG so they scale without blur. Print styles: omit interactive hover states, show plain text summaries. Keyboard: Tab order matches visual flow (KPIs→charts→tables), Enter opens Cycle Detail from any hovered bar.

acceptance_criteria: A new GET /api/projects/:pid/metrics/summary endpoint returns velocity (tickets/DONE per sprint), burn rate (USD per cycle phase and overall win rate), cost per outcome type (FEATURE vs BUG), and a 14-day trend indicator (improving/stable/regressing) for velocity and cost.
The dashboard Overview tab shows a condensed health panel with the four metrics above plus the three most common failure modes ranked by frequency, with a link to filter tickets by that mode.
A GET /api/projects/:pid/metrics/trends?days=N endpoint returns time-series data (day-by-day) for velocity, spend per phase, and failure count, usable by frontend line charts.

When a burn rate exceeds 2x the sprint average for any single phase over the last 5 completed cycles, the dashboard flags it with a warning badge on the Overview panel and posts an advisory to the #agents channel.
Edge case: If fewer than 3 completed cycles exist in history, trends show '(insufficient data)' and the trend indicator is omitted; the metrics endpoint returns success with null trend fields.

tickets.title: Pre-mortem Analysis — risk assessment before commitment
tickets.description:
The team already has a claim/release mechanism, a ready gate, and cost-approval gates. But when a ticket enters InProgress, there is no systematic pre-commit risk analysis beyond the SA's technical design. The SA assesses feasibility, the PO assesses cost — but no role answers the question 'if this ticket fails, why will it have failed?' A pre-mortem frames the discussion differently: by anticipating failure modes, the team can re-scope or add safeguards before burning cycles.

User problem: The PO commits tickets to a sprint based on priority and complexity but has no structured risk data. Tickets frequently blow past estimates because a real risk (dependency, integration, environment setup) was never surfaced before work started.

Value hypothesis: The PO gets one additional signal before sprint commitment — a structured risk assessment listing likely root causes of failure with severity. The SA and PD read this before design work begins, potentially adjusting the design to mitigate the top-2 risks. This reduces InProgress blowouts and re-opened bugs.

Product goal alignment: 'Cost-approval gate for expensive tickets' plus the claim/release safety mechanism — risk assessment is the missing input that makes the cost gate meaningful (high risk = higher expected cost).

Dependencies: Requires only the BA-to-agent interface on a ticket (no new data stores); the pre-mortem is a one-shot agent run that writes findings to a field on the Ticket or as attached analysis. Existing AgentEnginePort and prompt resolution from CXA-F001.
Risk: The pre-mortem is an agent-run operation that costs tokens. Must have a cheap-path option (deterministic risk heuristics from ticket metadata: complex tickets with dependencies flagged automatically) to avoid burning budget on low-complexity items.
acceptance_criteria: A POST /api/projects/:pid/ticket/:id/pre-mortem endpoint triggers a one-shot agent analysis that returns a structured JSON array of risk entries (risk_description: string, severity: High/Medium/Low, mitigation_suggestion: string), and attaches the result to the ticket's analysis section.
The pre-mortem is automatically triggered when PO or User clicks a 'Risk assess before sprint' action on a ticket in Pending or Ready status, before it enters InProgress.
The ticket detail view in the dashboard displays pre-mortem findings prominently above acceptance criteria, with a color-coded severity badge for each risk level.

Edge case: For tickets with complexity=Small, the system uses deterministic heuristics (if depends_on is non-empty, flag 'blocker risk'; if description exceeds 500 words without technical details, flag 'unclear scope risk') instead of invoking the agent, keeping cost near zero.
Edge case: If the pre-mortem agent fails, the ticket is not blocked — a warning note '(pre-mortem unavailable — review technical design)' is shown, and the PO can retry or skip.

tickets.title: Sprint Burndown with Earning Rate Tracking
tickets.description:
Scrum mode already exists with sprint commit, close, and velocity history. But the sprint view is a static record: it shows what was committed and what was completed, with no visualisation of progress toward the goal mid-sprint. There is no burndown or earned value tracking to tell the team whether they are on pace.

User problem: During a 2-week sprint, the PO has no visibility into whether the team is 'ahead' or 'behind schedule' beyond counting tickets. A sprint might look fine at mid-point (15 of 30 tickets committed, 7 done) but the 7 done could all be small chores while the hard features remain — a false sense of progress.

Value hypothesis: The PO sees a burndown chart (or earning-rate metric) during the sprint, enabling real-time course corrections: re-prioritise, re-scope, or request help. This is basic scrum practice that the team should have for informed decision-making.

Product goal alignment: 'Scrum & FinOps: Optional sprint mode (commit backlog, roll over, report velocity)' — earning rate is the natural extension of velocity reporting that turns historical data into live guidance. Also aligns with 'self-tuning' — poor sprint execution patterns feed back into backlog capacity planning.

Dependencies: Sprint data already exists in ProjectState (sprint: Option<Sprint>, sprints: Vec<SprintRecord>, sprint_goal, committed ticket IDs). The use case already advances sprints and tracks done counts.
Risk: Minimal — this is a reporting feature on top of existing data. The UI chart is the heaviest part, but the dashboard SPA already loads charting-capable JS assets.
acceptance_criteria: A GET /api/projects/:pid/sprint/burndown endpoint returns time-series data for the current active sprint: each tick records elapsed time (sprint day number), tickets_done count, and tickets_earned (estimated effort points — derived from ticket complexity: small=1, medium=2, large=3 — weighted by whether the ticket was completed in Full/Partial).

The Sprint dashboard view renders a burndown chart showing the ideal linear burn (from committed effort at day 0 to 0 at sprint end) vs actual earned effort, with a gap indicator (blue if ahead, red if behind, grey if on track within 10%).
When a sprint is not active (no sprint in progress), the endpoint and view show the last completed sprint's burndown retrospective.
Edge case: If the sprint has zero committed tickets, the burndown shows a flat line at zero with a '(no committed work)' note.
Edge case: If tickets are re-committed and de-committed during the sprint, the earned rate is recalculated at each commit/drop event and the chart updates from that new basis point.
