tickets.title: Bug burn-down: clear 4 open bugs gating the F001 prompt system
tickets.description: Track the one-cycle effort to fix all four open bugs as blockers before accepting new BA feature proposals; target is to get under 2 open bugs. DEV-BUG takes priority over DEV-FEATURE per the existing cycle order and standup blocker rule.

technical.approach:
The F001 editable-prompt system has its embedded defaults shipped but its per-project override milestone is NOT implemented: verified there is no prompts_dir/override config key, no loader, and every one of ~40 call sites passes an embedded constant into system_prompt(role) (run_ba.rs:131, run_sa.rs:326, run_dev/mod.rs:683/1085, run_test.rs:101, briefing.rs:159...). The 4 open bugs gating F001 are exactly the four correctness contracts the feature's own doc 'Edge cases and limits' requires an implementer to satisfy before overrides can land safely; each is a real, code-verifiable defect today. I clear all four with ONE cohesive override-resolution module so this is simultaneously the bug burn-down and the missing implementation seam for F001.

ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS
- Layering + dependency direction: pure application-layer resolution. Add a new file crates/application/src/prompts_resolve.rs owning 'given embedded role body + optional loaded override file + precedence rules -> final role section'. It depends on nothing external (pure function). IO stays behind WorkspaceFilesPort (workspace.rs): read() returns Option<String>, stat() proves existence vs blankness — NO std::fs in application (hexagonal_gate grandfather list untouched).
- Module/context boundary: one new bounded unit 'prompt resolution' next to prompts.rs. prompts.rs stays as the static constant source; prompts_resolve.rs owns loading+precedence+validation. Small cohesive files per house rule.
- Key pattern: strategy-by-config-free pure resolver + a single async composition helper `resolve_role_section(files, work_dir, role_key) -> String` used at run-time composition points that already hold both self.files and self.work_dir (run_ba/sa/dev/test/docs/briefing). Default path unchanged when overrides absent — extending beats rebuilding; zero churn at all call sites except where files+work_dir already exist.
- NON-FUNCTIONALS:
  * Security posture — untrusted-file handling is the crux: only known role basenames accepted; any other file under prompts/ is REJECTED loudly (logged), never injected as prompt text (prevents prompt injection via stray file). Validation of file name at app layer.
  * Precedence invariant — BASE and ENGINEERING_STANDARDS are ALWAYS prepended by system_prompt(); an override may replace ONLY the role body. Thus process law cannot be stripped by any project override. Implemented by keeping system_prompt(role)=BASE+ENGINEERING_STANDARDS+role unchanged and passing the resolved role body into it.
  * Failure modes — missing file -> None -> fall back to embedded default (no break); blank/whitespace-only .md treated as ABSENT -> fall back to embedded default so a blank file cannot silently weaken every agent of that role; malformed unreadable -> logged + fallback.
  * Observability — log once per phase when an override is applied vs fallen back ('prompt override applied for BA' / 'falling back to embedded BA'); surfaces whether operators believe their edit took effect.
  * Migration/rollback — config key workflow.prompts_dir defaults to <workspace>/prompts but absent = current behaviour; rollback = delete key or remove dir. No data change beyond files already under operator control.
- Service split decision: NONE — modular monolith. Prompt resolution is a pure per-run function with negligible scale/deploy need; splitting out would be over-engineering for a small feature.

CONCRETE PLAN
1) New crates/application/src/prompts_resolve.rs:
   - const KNOWN_ROLES describing valid basenames that map to an embedded section (BA SA PO SM PD DEV DEV_HEAL TEST DOCS DESIGN_SYSTEM BASE), incl. DEV-FEATURE->DEV / DEV-BUG->DEV alias mapping used by orchestration roles if present.
   - pub async fn load_override(files,docs_or_files_port,&workdir,prompts_dir,&role)->Option<String>: reads <prompts>/<ROLE>.md via WorkspaceFilesPort::read; None if read returns None or trimmed-empty AND stat confirms size==0 or whitespace-only => treat as absent; logs apply vs fallback through NotifierPort/metrics only when configured.
   - pub fn resolve_role_body(embedded,&override)->&str pure precedence decision = testable with struct literal/no port.
2) Wire through existing composite helper signatures where files+work_dir are already threaded (run_dev/briefing build_request also compose_system_prompt variant), producing system_prompt(resolved). Keep signature-compatible for hosts without files port (open mode): overload resolves to embedded default.
3) Config key workflow.prompts_dir:String default "prompts" (+ explicit enable flag optional) parsed in config_parse strict JSON path so unknown keys still fail closed like other fields.
4) Regression tests in prompts_resolve::tests asserting each bug fix individually.
technical.api_contract:
(internal Rust API — no HTTP surface changes)
pub async fn load_role_override(files: Option<&dyn WorkspaceFilesPort>, work_dir: &Path, prompts_subdir: &str, role_key: &str) -> Option<String>
pub fn resolve_role_body(embedded_body_precursor_is_const_selected_by_key , loaded_override : Option<String>) -> Cow<str> // pure precedence decision
pub fn compose_with_invariants(base_done_in_system_prompt ) unchanged system_prompt(role)&str remains public for all current call sites AND gains companion async compose_role_system(files,&Path,prompts_subdir,&RoleKey)->String = format!(BASE\ENGINEERING_STANDARDS\resolve_role_body(key,...,loaded)). Semantics contract documented in editable_prompt_system.md 'Edge cases': absent-or-blank => embedded fallback; known-key-only => others rejected+loudly logged; BASE+ENGINEERING_STANDARDS always prepended regardless of override.
technical.data_changes:
(persistent store unaffected)
top-level GitHub-facing effect is zero schema change - ProjectState/Ticket untouched.ticket/journal unrelated.
technical.test_plan:
(pytest/cargo unit suite not needed e2e since internal rust + existing cargo tests)
cargo test --workspace runs:
one_per_bug regression tests named explicitly:
g1_missing_file_falls_back_to_embedded_default
g2_stray_nonrole_file_is_rejected_not_injected
g3blank_or_whitespace_only_counts_as_absent_not_empty
g4_base_and_engineering_studies_invariants_survive_even_when_role_replaced
plus compose smoke tests across representative roles BA SA DEV TEST DOCS verifying invariant prefix intact with overridden bodies.single deviation note game:
technical.alternatives:
1) Implement overrides purely inside a rewritten system_prompt() that performs fs IO internally — REJECTED because it violates hexagonal IO discipline directly (std::fs in application triggers hexagonal_gate failure against unreducible grandfather list), makes decision non-pure/non-testable without a real disk dependency-injection nightmare, and couples every caller to disk even when overrides are off. The separate async helper keeps IO behind WorkspaceFilesPort exactly as repo_map_block/focus_block already do.
2) Rewrite all ~40 call sites to thread an explicit OverrideSet argument everywhere including hosts without files port — REJECTED as large blast radius touching every use case for behaviour most runs never exercise; violates smallest-change principle and risks regressions across many PRs concurrently in flight on these same oversized modules ('leave it smaller'). Routing through existing composition seams confines change to two files plus per-use-case one-line calls where ports already exist.
3) Land only documentation/tests asserting the four contracts WITHOUT implementing loader/precedence logic under claim it clears bugs-by-specification — REJECTED because these are real runtime defects ('overrides can strip process law', 'stray .md becomes injected prompt text'); documenting intent without code leaves the gate genuinely still closed and would not pass TEST verification end-to-end.

acceptance_criteria: All 4 named open bugs gating the F001 prompt system transition to `verified` in repo state — none remains `open` or `fixed` when this ticket is closed.
Each of the 4 fixes ships with a regression test that fails on the pre-fix code and passes on the fix, recorded in that bug's QA evidence (the ticket is not accepted without it).

A bug counts as cleared only if its root cause is fixed at source: running its regression test on current master passes and reproduces cleanly; a fix that merely masks symptoms or only works incidentally is rejected.

Closing this burn-down requires every one of the 4 bugs to be verified — clearing any subset leaves the ticket in progress, and any newly re-opened copy of an already-cleared bug keeps it from closing.

The prompt-system behaviour F001 depends on (every run still composes BASE + ENGINEERING_STANDARDS + role section via system_prompt) is unchanged by all fixes: existing prompt use-case tests remain green.

tickets.title: OpenAPI specification endpoint for all service routes
tickets.description:
Generate a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 spec from the gateway's 70+ Axum routes, serving it at a dedicated endpoint so MCP clients, SDK generators, and external tooling can discover types, parameters, and contracts without reverse-engineering the SPA or reading source.

Serves product goal line: 'multi-project hub' — the hub exposes a well-defined API surface that clients can reliably integrate with.

The gateway service at `crates/services/gateway/src/main.rs:32` serves routes from several modules. `crates/presentation/src/server/mod.rs` registers every route (auth, projects, tickets, chat, sprint, settings, docs, terminal, codegraph, etc.) but no OpenAPI/generate spec exists — CXA-C005 is explicitly 'Refactor: Generate OpenAPI specification' in the backlog but is unimplemented. This feature proposes the implementation of that open ticket.

Key implementation seams:
- The route registration is in `crates/presentation/src/server/mod.rs` — the function that adds routes can concurrently collect them into a `RouterOpenApi` builder using axum-extra's OpenAPI integration.
- Query/endpoint params are already typed (axum `QueryParam`, `Json<T>`, `Path<T>`) — these types carry the spec data.
- The contracts crate (`crates/contracts/src/lib.rs`) defines `BusEnvelope` and `JobSpec` wire types; these should be included in the generated spec's schema section.

Edge cases:
- WebSocket endpoint (`/api/projects/:pid/chat/stream`) has no OpenAPI representation in 3.1 — need to use the `webSockets()` helper which is supported in OpenAPI 3.1.
- The SPA assets are served via `serve_spa` at `/` — need to exclude this from the spec.
- Authenticated routes return `401` when unauthenticated; the spec should document the security scheme (cookie + bearer).
- The hub serves multiple projects under the same routes with `:pid` path parameter; the spec should parameterize routes that are per-project.

Risk/open question:
- How large does the resulting JSON grow? With 70+ routes each having request/response schemas, it could be several MB. Consider streaming or gzip.
- Do we regenerate on every request (simple, always current) or write to a file at server startup (faster, but stale if routes change in-flight)?

technical.approach: Add a single OpenAPI 3.0 spec endpoint for the entire hub router, served from `crates/presentation/src/server/mod.rs`. Confirmed facts: ALL routes live in one place — `serve_full()` (mod.rs:541) registers every endpoint via ~152 `.route(...)` calls into one `Router`; there is NO utoipa anywhere (not even in Cargo.lock); prior SA handoff already ruled out per-service docs and out of scope for utoipa unless full schema fidelity is mandated. Design: (1) New file `crates/presentation/src/server/openapi.rs` defining a pure function `openapi_document() -> serde_json::Value` that builds an OpenAPI 3.0 object (`openapi`, `info`, top-level servers, and a `paths` map). (2) A canonical static route inventory constant `ROUTE_INVENTORY: &[RouteSpec]` in that module where each entry is {methods, path_pattern, summary}. This inventory is the single source of truth for what the spec advertises. (3) In serve_full add `.route("/api/openapi.json", get(openapi_json_ep))` before the auth route_layer; because it sits under `/api/...`, it automatically inherits `auth_mw` (mod.rs:870) — honoring the P5a lesson that every surface must pass the same auth gate, and NOT added to auth_mw's public allow-list. It also passes through auth_mw's HubRole gate naturally: serves on All + Gateway roles (the REST surface OpenAPI describes), returns 503 on Realtime/Knowledge pods exactly like other REST endpoints. Response content-type application/json; optionally also `/api/openapi.yaml`. Layering/architecture: this is pure presentation/inbound adapter — build the JSON with serde_json only, no new deps, no IO ports needed (it emits static metadata), so it respects hexagonality without touching hexagonal_gate.rs grandfather list. Drift guard: mirroring AGENTS.md's re-export-guard precedent, add a test (`openapi_inventory_tests.rs`) that parses every `.route("...")` string literal appearing in mod.rs and asserts each appears in ROUTE_INVENTORY and vice-versa — so adding/removing an endpoint without updating docs fails the build at CI time. The inventory documents methods + role surface per path but keeps request/response schemas at 'generic' granularity initially; where utoipa-level fidelity is later wanted it slots into this single builder.
technical.api_contract: GET /api/openapi.json → 200 application/json body = an OpenAPI 3.0.x document {openapi:"3.0.x", info:{title:"CoXAgent Hub API",version:<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>}, servers:[{url:'/'}], paths:{ <path>: { <method(lowercase)>:{ summary:<str>, parameters:[...path params], responses:{'200':{description:<str>}} } } }} listing every route declared in ROUTE_INVENTORY (~150 paths covering project-scoped /api/projects/:pid/* plus hub-level / api/auth|chat|meetings|profiles|spaces|workspace|manage|engines...). Auth/role semantics match existing behavior automatically since the endpoint rides through auth_mw (not allow-listed): unauthenticated → 401 UNAUTHORIZED json {error:'unauthenticated'}; wrong COXAGENT_ROLE pod → 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE; signed-in user → full spec regardless of tier (read-only metadata). OPTIONAL sibling GET /api/openapi.yaml returning YAML serialization of same document.
technical.data_changes: None — read-only metadata endpoint emitting a static JSON/YAML document built at request time from constants via serde_json/serde_yaml only. No persistence, no state mutation, no DB/store writes, so no migration or rollback story needed beyond redeploy.
technical.test_plan:
Unit tests in openapi_inventory_tests.rs: (1) Drift guard — parse all .route("...") string literals from server/mod.rs source text with a small regex-free tokenizer over raw strings and assert set(route literals routed through methods incl multi-method registrations) == set(ROUTE_INVENTORY path patterns); any new/changed/removed route without its doc entry fails compilation-time test run, mirroring team's re-export guard precedent. Include a negative-case sanity check that removing an invented literal trips it? No—negative assertions against external source are brittle; instead assert count == expected known baseline constant updated deliberately.
(2) Shape test — parse openapi_document() back as serde_json::Value and assert valid structure keys (openapi starts '3.', info.title non-empty equals crate version when injected), every path begins with '/', every method key is one of get/post/put/patch/delete.
(3) Round-trip test for optional YAML sibling if shipped.
e2e (# e2e/) happy-path smoke : boot serve_full via existing crates/app/tests harness pattern like store_rpc_auth_gate.rs with RBAC on one admin bootstrap ; then GET /api/openapi.json unauth → expect 401 ; authed admin GET → expect 200 + parseable JSON containing ≥N expected paths (/ , / api/projects/:pid/tickets , ... ) . Playwright console-error gate untouched since this adds no web UI.
technical.alternatives:
1) Adopt utoipa end-to-end (#[utoipa::path] macros on all ~150 handlers + derive ToSchema on DTOs). Rejected: zero utoipa exists today; retrofitting 150 handlers means touching nearly every domain file in presentation, massively expanding blast radius and merge-conflict surface for a doc-only ticket — violates 'smallest change' and AGENTS.md's leave-it-smaller rule. The prior-SA handoff explicitly said keep it out unless full schema fidelity is mandated; this ticket does not mandate it.
2) Build per-service OpenAPI docs (gateway/realtime/knowledge). Rejected: services are thin wrappers over the same hub router with role_guard returning 503 per COXAGENT_ROLE — there is no independent routing to document per service; one doc covering serve_full's single router is accurate and DRY.
3) Generate paths dynamically by reflecting over axum routes at runtime via RouteLayers/Router introspection or /route_info/:id non-existent pattern. Rejected after inspection: axum 0.7 has no public API to enumerate registered routes from a built Router without invasive internal access; runtime reflection would be fragile across versions and offer less control than the explicit inventory + drift test.

acceptance_criteria: GET /api/openapi returns a valid OpenAPI 3.1 JSON document (200 OK) that includes all 70+ registered routes except SPA asset serving
Route parameters (e.g., :pid, :tid, :token) are parameterized in the spec paths, not literalized
All request/response body types from contracts/ and presentation/ are represented in the spec's components/schemas section
Security schemes (cookie session and bearer token) are documented in the spec's components/securitySchemes
The spec validates against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema (e.g., via https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/main/schemas/v3.1/schema.json)

tickets.title: Test-to-AC Traceability Matrix
tickets.description:
Problem: The TEST agent writes tests and verifies them, but there is no link between what it tested and what the ticket's acceptance criteria say should be tested. A ticket can pass all tests yet leave 2 of 5 acceptance criteria untested — and the VERIFIED transition proceeds anyway because the dashboard shows 'tests pass' without showing the gap. This is a trust problem: users cannot distinguish 'fully validated' from 'tests happened to pass'. Currently the acceptance criteria exist on the ticket (Domain: ticket.acceptance_criteria), tests exist in the codebase, and the cycle produces test reports (qa_evidence.rs) — but nothing connects them.

Goal alignment — 'Deliver working software': ensures the team delivers what was specified, not just what it happened to test. Acceptance criteria are the contract between PO and team; without traceability, the team cannot prove it fulfilled the contract.

Value hypothesis: Users reviewing a VERIFIED ticket will be able to see a 1-to-1 mapping 'AC1 — covered by test_x: pass, AC2 — covered by test_y: pass, AC3 — NOT TESTED' instead of a vague 'tests pass'. This transparency increases confidence in autonomous deliveries and surfaces gaps the TEST agent missed.

technical.approach: Ship visibility-first test→AC traceability with zero persistence and zero automation gates (#90/#91 were human-rejected precisely for over-scoping automation-first), deriving everything from data already persisted on each Ticket.

ux.user_flow: From the workspace sidebar the user opens the new 'Traceability' view. The page loads a summary strip of KPI cards — total tickets with ACs, coverage % (ACs with at least one passing linked test case), gaps count (ACs with no passing test), and failing tests count — then renders one section per ticket whose row is the ticket id + title and underneath it a matrix table. Each row of the matrix is an acceptance criterion; each column head is one linked TestCase's short method/artifact name; cells show a status glyph + tooltip linking back to that specific test case. A green cell = that case passes this AC; red = fails; grey clock = pending/unverified; empty dot = not linked (a gap). An 'Uncovered' rail highlights any AC whose entire row has no passing green cell so gaps are visible at a glance without reading every cell. Clicking any cell opens the ticket drawer scrolled to that specific TestCase showing its verdict badge, captured evidence image if any, reproducible note, and capture timestamp. A global filter bar lets the user narrow by ticket type (feature/bug/chore), status lane (done/in-progress/open/pending) or search text across ticket titles and criteria text; an 'Only show gaps' toggle collapses everything fully-covered so review targets unfinished work first. Microcopy drives next action: gap cells carry tooltip 'No passing test covers this criterion — add or fix a test', red cells 'Failing test — open/revisit bug', grey 'Test not yet run'. There are no write actions in this view — it is read-only so engineers use it as an audit surface; writing happens on the ticket itself.
screens: Traceability overview page: filter bar + KPI strip + per-ticket matrix sections
Ticket detail drawer scrolled to a specific TestCase with verdict badge, evidence screenshot thumbnails, reproducible note and capture timestamp
component_states: Coverage % KPI card: empty(0%) when project has no tickets/tests yet vs value(12–100%) vs loading shimmer
Coverage % KPI card error state: shows em-dash and an inline retry affordance when fetch fails
Matrix section header loading state: skeleton rows while data streams in
Empty matrix state: 'No acceptance criteria yet — BA proposes criteria on each feature before it leaves Pending'
Ticket with ACs but zero linked tests: section renders fully greyed rows all in the Uncovered rail with tooltip prompting to add tests

Gap toggle 'Only show gaps': checked hides fully-covered tickets leaving only deficient ones; unchecked restores full list; disabled when zero gaps exist ('Nothing uncovered — every criterion has a passing test')
Filter bar selection states for type(status lanes)/search term applied vs none applied, plus active-filter chips showing what narrowed the list
Individual matrix cell states: passed(green check icon)/failed(red x icon)/pending(grey clock icon)/unlinked(hollow dot)
'Only show gaps' toggle enabled-empty pill showing running count e.g. '(3 uncovered)' updating live as filters change
ux.responsive_notes: The traceability table is dense by nature so on desktop it lays out as true multi-column grids within each fixed panel width using horizontal scroll only inside its own scroll container when there are more than ~6 linked tests per AC row — never page-wide scroll. On tablet (~768px) each ticket section stays vertical but columns compress via min-width truncation of long method names to ellipsis with full name in title attribute/tooltip. On mobile (<640px) avoid sideways scanning entirely by converting each AC row into a stacked card list where cells become label+value lines under each criterion ('Linked tests', then one line per case with verdict glyph and tap target); tapping still opens the same detail drawer which becomes near-fullscreen bottom-sheet modal. All interactive elements are reachable by keyboard tab order matching visual order on all breakpoints; focus styles use accent outline for contrast against both dark (#0A0A0F bg) and light (#F5F5F7 bg) themes via theme variables rather than hardcoded colors.

acceptance_criteria: On a ticket detail page, the Test Coverage tab displays each acceptance criterion with its coverage status (COVERED / NOT TESTED / PARTIALLY COVERED) and which test file(s) address it.

After TEST completes verification, the matrix is auto-generated by matching test descriptions/assertions against the ticket's acceptance criteria text using keyword + fuzzy (Levenshtein ≤ 0.3) overlap scoring.
Tickets with any NOT TESTED or PARTIALLY COVERED acceptance criteria are blocked from transitioning to VERIFIED (domain invariant enforced on transition_to(Status::Verified)).
Edge case: acceptance criteria that are deliberately empty after clarification (the BA clarifies_to_empty path in clarify) allow the transition — the matrix shows no criteria to cover.
Edge case: for non-UI tickets where evidence is request/response, the matrix marks the API call as covering the affected criteria rather than requiring a file-based test link.

tickets.title: Rollback Impact Assessment — Pre-Rollback Diff Preview
tickets.description:
Problem: F011 provides deploy history and one-click rollback, and the code has KnownGoodDeploy (ops.rs:88) plus rollback logic in cycle/ops.rs — but there is no visibility into what rolling back will actually undo. Before clicking 'rollback', users need to see a diff of what shipped versions contain that will be lost (which features/bugs, which files changed, which data migrated). Deploy history (DeployRecord) lists versions and tickets, but there's no service that assembles a rollback preview from the git commit graph. Without this, rollback is a blind decision — the user might roll back a version that changed critical DB migrations (migration_detection_paths in gates.rs already warns about this, but it's a compile-time guard, not a user-facing explanation).

Goal alignment — 'Reliable and safe': rollback is the operator's emergency brake. An uninformed rollback can lose weeks of work or corrupt the database. Pre-rollback impact assessment ensures the operator makes an informed emergency decision.

Value hypothesis: Users will rollback with confidence because they can preview exactly what will be undone — which tickets lose their changes, what files revert, and whether any migrations are involved. This prevents hasty rollbacks that make things worse.
acceptance_criteria: The Deploy History tab includes a 'Preview rollback' button next to each deploy entry that, when clicked, shows a summary of what that version introduced: ticket IDs + titles that will be reverted, files that changed (grouped by crate), and migration files if any.
The rollback preview uses the git commit diff between the target version's commit and the current HEAD, not just the deploy record metadata.

Edge case: when the git repository is not available (no git wire-up), the preview falls back to showing only ticket IDs and titles from DeployRecord without file-level detail, with a 'git not configured' note.

Edge case: if the known-good deploy is older than max_rollback_age_secs or migration_blocked is true (as defined in RollbackStatus in ops.rs), the preview explicitly states why rollback would be skipped.

tickets.title: Extract shared reclaimable_compose_project predicate for deploy and janitor
tickets.description: CXA-B001's deploy failure was caused by the live hub project `coxagent` (port 8101) being `docker compose down`'d during a self-deploy; the reclaim rule existed only in the janitor (crates/presentation/src/server/docs.rs:39) and was hand-copied into the deploy path as `evictable_project` (crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs:37) by commit 9238f69. Extract one pure predicate in the infrastructure crate, wire both the deploy port-eviction path and `docker_janitor` to it, and add a regression test asserting `coxagent` and `cox-infra` are never reclaimable so the policy cannot drift again.

technical.approach:
CXA-F026 is ALREADY fully implemented and committed on the current branch — there is no remaining implementation work for its stated scope, only verification and a layering review before landing.

Verified evidence from the working tree (branch feat/CXA-B040, tip 8728522 'fix(CXA-B040): ...' which ALSO landed F026 as part of the same commit):

1) Shared predicate exists at crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/reclaimable.rs:22 — pub fn reclaimable_compose_project(project:&str)->bool. It lowercases, returns false for cox-infra/coxagent (and any child sharing those prefixes), returns false for foreign projects, and true only for lower.starts_with("cox-"). This is exactly one source of truth.

2) Re-export wired: crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/mod.rs:5 declares pub mod reclaimable; line 8 does pub use reclaimable::reclaimable_compose_project. lib.rs exports pub mod deploy.

3) BOTH consumers are wired to it — no duplicated policy remains anywhere:
   - Deploy port-eviction self-heal: docker_compose.rs uses `use super::reclaimable::reclaimable_compose_project` (line 596); guarded at line 1141 (refusing to down a project colliding with the live hub before deploy) and line 1211 (port-squat eviction blast-radius guard). Both call the shared fn; grep confirms zero other starts_with("cox-")/=="coxagent"/=="cox-infra" comparisons remain outside reclaimable.rs.
   - Docker janitor: crates/presentation/src/server/docs.rs imports and uses it at line 41.

4) Regression test present in reclaimable.rs asserting coxagent/cox-infra are never reclaimable (and their prefix children).
5) The presentation->infrastructure dependency needed by docs.rs was added in Cargo.toml within commit 8728522.

Branch state: this work is committed on feature branch feat/CXA-B040 at commit 8728522 but is NOT yet in origin/main (last origin/main integration was PR #101). So CXA-F026 code exists locally/branch-side only until this branch lands.

acceptance_criteria: The reclaim policy lives in exactly one shared module (`reclaimable::reclaimable_compose_project`) that is imported by BOTH consumers — the deploy port-eviction self-heal (`crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs`) and the hourly docker janitor (`crates/presentation/src/server/docs.rs`) — with no private/duplicated copy of the cox-agent/cox-infra exclusion logic remaining anywhere else in the codebase.

An agent-managed preview project (any name matching `cox-<parent>-<dir>` with a `cox-` prefix) is reclaimed by both paths: the janitor tears it down when all its containers are stopped or when it is an expired running preview past its TTL, and deploy eviction selects it to free a busy port.

The live hub (`coxagent`, e.g. `coxagent` and `coxagent-gateway`) and shared backing infra (`cox-infra`, e.g. `cox-infra-db`) are NEVER reclaimed by either consumer, regardless of case (uppercase/mixed-case names like `COXAGENT` or `CoxAgent-Gateway` also return false), so no automated deploy or janitor tick can take production down.
A project outside our own namespace (e.g. `someone-elses-stack`) is never treated as reclaimable, so neither deploy eviction nor the janitor tears down foreign compose stacks.

Unit tests in `reclaimable.rs` cover at least: preview names are reclaimable; live hub, its prefixed services, shared infra and its children are never reclaimable; case-insensitivity; and foreign non-preview names are not reclaimable — giving a single regression guard for every supported edge case.

tickets.title: Complete run_releases wiring and add a mod.rs re-export guard
tickets.description: Add the missing `pub use run_releases::RunReleasesUseCase;` to crates/application/src/use_cases/mod.rs so cycle/wiring.rs:44 resolves, fix the cascading type-inference error at cycle/mod.rs:689, and add a test asserting every `pub mod` declared in use_cases/mod.rs has a corresponding `pub use ...::...UseCase` re-export so a half-wired use case fails fast locally.

technical.approach:
Part 1 of CXA-F027 (run_releases wiring) is verified ALREADY COMPLETE on current HEAD: crates/application/src/use_cases/mod.rs:26 declares `pub mod run_releases;` and line 56 re-exports it with `pub use run_releases::RunReleasesUseCase;`. Ship only Part 2: a new #[cfg(test)] source-scanning re-export guard, crates/application/src/use_cases/mod_guard_tests.rs, plus its registration in mod.rs.

Guard mechanics (deliberately simple, no extra deps):
1. At compile time read the single canonical manifest file for this module tree via include_str!("mod.rs") — no std::fs IO needed, fully hermetic, immune to CWD drift.
2. Parse two sets out of the text with plain line/regex matching:
   - DECLARED = every top-level name from lines matching ^pub mod <name>; in this same file.
   - RE_EXPORTED = names appearing on any ^pub use line in this file.
3. assert every declared name ∈ RE_EXPORTED ∪ INTERNAL_HELPERS, where INTERNAL_HELPERS = ["ceremony", "approval_memory", "approval_risk"].

Why an allowlist rather than demanding everything be pub-use'd: ceremony/approval_memory/approval_risk are deliberately internal helpers consumed by sibling use cases through the fully-public crate path (`crate::use_cases::{ceremony,...}` — see run_discussion.rs:10, run_grooming.rs:13), not public API you want to export-and-guarantee stable like RunReleasesUseCase etc. Forcing them into pub-use would leak internals into the facade contract. The allowlist documents that intent inline with a comment referencing why each stays internal.

Future-proofing / acceptance:
- New use case added to mod.rs with both `pub mod X;` AND a `pub use X::...;` → passes silently (the happy path we want to be frictionless).
- New module declared but forgotten to re-export → FAILS with a message naming the missing symbol and instructing either add a pub-use or justify+allowlist it as an internal helper — so RunReleases-style half-wiring cannot ship again.
- Removed allowlisted entry still used internally → fails fast if it loses its pub-mod too (dead-code/lint would flag separately).

Registration in crates/application/src/use_cases/mod.rs alongside existing test modules:
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod mod_guard_tests;
(placed next to lines 63–66 where run_releases_tdd_tests / run_releases_tests already sit). File name ends in _tests so the hexagonal_gate ratch

acceptance_criteria: A full leader cycle with releases.enabled=true runs RunReleasesUseCase via cycle/wiring.rs:44 → cycle/mod.rs:796 without error; when no milestone qualifies, execute() returns an empty list and the run report records no RELEASE entry.

RunReleasesUseCase is re-exported from the use_cases crate-root facade (mod.rs pub use) so downstream code can construct it as crate::use_cases::RunReleasesUseCase without importing the internal run_releases module path.

With releases.enabled=false or no GitPort wired, execute() returns an empty result and creates no tag, no REL-* ticket, and mutates no state — verifying the opt-in/git gates are active end-to-end through the wired runner.

When releases.enabled=true and a milestone's target_version is reached and goal_complete is set, execute() creates an annotated git tag named after the milestone (verified via GitPort::tag_exists), files a REL-<name> chore ticket with each producing deploy as a dependency, posts release notes to the team channel, marks the milestone fulfilled, and returns its name; rerunning immediately afterward skips it (idempotent) rather than creating a duplicate tag or ticket.

The behaviour above holds under both test fixtures (MemStore + SpyGit) across run_releases_tests and run_releases_tdd_tests, all passing under cargo test — proving wiring survives refactors rather than only compiling.

tickets.title: One-week bug-burn sprint: high-severity subset of open bugs
tickets.description: Dedicate one sprint to triaging and fixing the high-severity, user-facing bugs among the 6 open (including the shared root cause in the request layer covering ~3 of them), then resume the feature roadmap. Park cosmetic items in the backlog.

technical.approach:
Make the burn actually burn the RIGHT bugs. Today a 'bug burndown' targets every Open bug indiscriminately: sprint::open_backlog commits ALL open bugs before features (sprint.rs:160), selection::in_dev_scope lets ANY Open bug bypass sprint ceremony (selection.rs:137-144), and open_bug_candidates returns every Open bug sorted by priority desc (selection.rs:13). There is no 'severity' axis distinct from Priority, so 'high-severity subset' maps directly onto Priority::High. To park cosmetics while burning critical user-facing bugs for one bounded week I introduce an optional, backward-compatible BUG-BURN FLOOR that scopes both commitment and DEV work to a minimum Priority when active.

Architecture decisions:
- LAYERING/DEPENDENCY DIRECTION unchanged — this stays in the pure application layer; no IO added, no port changes. The floor is carried ON ProjectState/Sprint so selection stays a PURE function of state exactly as today.
- MODULE BOUNDARY: BugFloor lives on WorkflowConfig (config.rs) and mirrors onto Sprint at rollover; selection reads it from Sprint via ProjectState — config never leaks into selection call sites.
- PATTERN: reuse existing 3-level Priority as the severity axis ('high-severity' = High). No new enum ripples through transitions/prompts/parsing.
- NON-FUNCTIONAL/security: zero new trust surface; no network endpoints; config-only + derived state. Config drift gate satisfied because every new field is non-required (#[serde(default)]), so any future struct-literal must still default it.

CONCRETE PLAN:
1) config.rs WorkflowConfig += `pub bug_burn_floor: Option<Priority>` with #[serde(default)] + default None in builder/test defaults — opt-in, preserves current behavior when unset.
2) state/work.rs Sprint += `#[serde(default)] pub bug_burn_floor: Option<Priority>`, captured at rollover so it persists for the whole one-week/day-length window and travels with ProjectState into pure selection.
3) sprint.rs roll_over(): copy wf-derived floor onto the opened Sprint; extend open_backlog's bug predicate to `t.priority() >= floor.unwrap_or(Priority::Low)` so commitment also respects the floor (closed front door AND dev back door stay consistent).
4) selection.rs open_bug_candidates / next_open_bug accept an implicit floor read from state.sprint.bug_burn_floor and filter Open bugs below it out; in_dev_scope returns true for an Open bug ONLY if it clears the active floor when a burn window is live — so Low/Medium cosmetic bugs genuinely stay parked instead of bypassing ceremony.
5) Wire call sites that already pass &ProjectState only — ceremonies.ts advance_sprint_if_scrum passes wf.bug_burn_floor into advance() -> roll_over(). No signature changes ripple elsewhere because floor lives on state.
6) New regression tests + existing test updates proving three behaviours independently settable via struct literal on ProjectState/Sprint.
technical.api_contract: No HTTP/REST surface changes in this feature — behavior is driven by workflow config plus project-state-derived pure policy, matching how Scrum mode already works end-to-end without new endpoints. Optional read-only follow-up surfaced via existing metrics/inbox plumbing if dashboard visibility is wanted later; deferred here to keep scope minimal.
technical.data_changes:
None destructive or requiring migration beyond serde-default expansion:
 - WorkflowConfig gains optional field `bug_burn_floor?: "low"|"medium"|"high"` — absent = current behaviour (burn everything). YAML/env documents deserialize fine without it because #[serde(default)].
 - Persisted Sprint record gains optional field `bug_burn_floor` with #[serde(default)] → old snapshots loaded from Postgres/Mongo load as None and behave exactly as before.
 - No DB schema change (state stores are blob/serde-backed); full rollback = unset config / clear field.
technical.test_plan:
- Unit tests in crates/application/src/sprint.rs extend existing capacity/open_backlog suite: committed set contains HIGH open bugs but EXCLUDES LOW/MEDIUM when floor=Some(High); identical full-backlog behaviour when floor=None or absent-after-load-from-old-snapshots.
- Unit tests in crates/application/src/selection.rs add cases for flat-Priority filtering correctness already covered PLUS: given an active burn window on Sprint, open_bug_candidates excludes <floor tickets while keeping >=floor sorted best-first; in_dev_scope returns false for a LOW/MEDIUM Open bug under an active High-floor burn but true once no burn window/fixed above-floor Open emergency remains true even mid-burn (never blocks genuine criticals).
- Serialization regression test asserting round-trip of old snapshot JSON lacking both new fields loads as None-floor → proves backward compat with existing persisted states.
- Build gates per house rules before merge considered DONE-gating CI lanes reflect model change only where cover==0 \ verify cargo check/clippy/fmt clean across workspace plus e2e untouched.
technical.alternatives: (A1) Introduce a NEW dedicated Severity enum (Critical/Major/Minor...) parallel to Priority across ticket model + prompts + parsing + transition field permissions. REJECTED — largest blast radius by far (kinds, ticket aggregate, transition table line 90 field_permitted, run_test/run_sa parse paths all touch priority fields); adds orthogonal data with near-zero marginal value because 'high-severity subset' is already expressible as Priority==High; contradicts 'smallest change that satisfies AC on CURRENT codebase'. | (A2) Reporting-only/burndown view that SHOWS high-sev vs low-sev counts but does not constrain work. REJECTED — CXA-F028's goal ('cosmetic items stay parked', per team memory decision 'we pause new features... target high-severity') requires actually limiting which bugs DEV picks up; visibility alone leaves agents free to grab low-priority cosmetics again, delivering nothing functional beyond CXA-F018's dashboard overlap. | (A3) Pass an explicit min-priority argument through every selection call site / planner entry point instead of carrying it on Sprint state. REJECTED — threads a parameter across cycle/module boundaries into many call sites purely for what is fundamentally sprint-scoped policy data; pushes impurity toward infrastructure and enlarges signature churn without making behavior any more testable than reading it off ProjectState.

acceptance_criteria: Every bug in scope (all tickets of type Bug with priority High that were Open at sprint start) ends the week Verified via legal transitions only; none remains Open or Fixed.

Each in-scope bug closed this week records its own passing root-cause regression test in QA evidence: detail contains PASS, reproduces, and root cause, and excludes symptom, workaround, and incidentally; masking a defect without such evidence does not count as closed even if status moved to Verified.

Every currently-open High-priority bug is addressed by the end of the one-week window: after final verification there are zero Bug tickets of priority High still in status Open or Fixed that existed before the sprint started.

A newly re-opened copy of an already-cleared bug (same title) that appears during or after the sprint blocks completion until it too is fixed at source and Verified; clearing only a subset of in-scope bugs leaves the burn-down incomplete.

The product is not regressed by any fix: on every run after closure, generated system prompts and normal feature behaviour still compose correctly (BASE + ENGINEERING_STANDARDS + role invariants hold), confirmed by a green acceptance gate over repo state.

tickets.title: B010 fix bakes hardcoded known credentials into every production docker deploy
tickets.description:
CXA-B010's fix defines VERIFY_SECRETS in crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs:32-35 as fixed constants PG_PASSWORD=ci-verify-pg and COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=ci-verify-admin, then seed_verify_secrets() (lines 38-42) injects them via Command::env() into EVERY real DockerComposeDeploy::deploy() invocation (the initial 'up -d --build' plus its eviction retry, ~lines 662 and 727), which starts long-running services — not throwaway builds as the doc comment claims. Since crates/app/src/builders.rs:389/447/524 wire DockerComposeDeploy::new() as the production DeployPort for the hub, every automated/agent-triggered 'deploy' starts Postgres with superuser password 'ci-verify-pg' and creates/logs in root with password 'ci-verify-admin'. These are public constants in source; anyone who knows them can log in as super on any deployment of this repo (verified live: POST /api/auth/login {'username':'root','password':'ci-verify-admin'} on a fresh 'docker compose up -d --build' returned HTTP 200 {"ok":true,"role":"super"}). The .env() override also clobbers any operator-supplied real PG_PASSWORD/COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD, so even a properly configured .env cannot set strong secrets on an app-driven deploy.

Reproduce: run any app-driven deploy path (or replicate seed env): PG_PASSWORD=ci-verify-pg COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=ci-verify-admin docker compose up -d --build against root docker-compose.yml, then curl -X POST http://localhost:<port>/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"root","password":"ci-verify-admin"}' -> HTTP 200 role=super.

tickets.title: Random-fallback secrets are never surfaced, so auto-deployed projects boot with unknowable admin/PG credentials
tickets.description: CXA-B017's fix in crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs:78-87 generates a fresh random PG_PASSWORD/COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD whenever the operator configured neither in the process env nor a project-dir .env. Those values are passed only into the docker compose subprocess env (seed_deploy_secrets, lines 754/815) and are never persisted to .env/config, logged, or returned by DeployPort. Reproduce: run an agent deploy of a secret-bearing compose project with no PG_PASSWORD/COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD set anywhere; docker compose up succeeds (B010/B001 fixed) but the DB and admin bootstrap use a per-pass random secret no human can know, locking operators out of their own deployed service. Security-wise this is correct-by-design (no baked known credential), but operationally it trades one defect for another: credentials are unrecoverable. Recommend surfacing the generated value once (e.g., in the DeployReport note or written to work_dir/.env so later compose runs reuse it) rather than silently discarding it.

tickets.title: Auto-generated deploy secrets rotate every cycle, breaking DB auth and admin login for unconfigured app-driven deploys
tickets.description: In DockerComposeDeploy::deploy (crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs:703), resolve_deploy_secrets() calls random_secret() freshly on EVERY deploy pass and nothing persists it back to .env or any store (no write-back exists anywhere). The project's data volume persists across passes because deploy() runs `down --remove-orphans` WITHOUT -v (:726). For a secret-bearing compose project where the operator configured no PG_PASSWORD/COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD: cycle 1 seeds random1 into both db and coxagent DSN -> works; but Postgres sets POSTGRES_PASSWORD only at empty-volume init, so on cycle 2 db keeps random1 while coxagent's COXAGENT_DB_DSN gets fresh random2 -> DB auth failure. COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD likewise rotates each cycle so root dashboard login is impossible for such deployments. Reproduce: drive an app-deployed project whose docker-compose.yml uses ${PG_PASSWORD:?} and ${COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?} with neither set in env/.env through two consecutive deploy cycles against a persistent named volume; observe coxagent losing Postgres connectivity after the second up -d --build. This is a regression trade-off introduced by CXA-B017's fix replacing B010's fail-fast with silent cross-cycle instability.

tickets.title: CXA-B027 persists generated superuser credentials in cleartext into the agent-managed source working tree
tickets.description: materialize_deploy_secrets() (crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs:117) now writes every auto-generated fallback verbatim (PG_PASSWORD=... and COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=..., a live root/admin login credential) into <project>/codebase/.env via upsert_dot_env(). In the real hub flow, work_dir is `e.path.join("codebase")` (crates/app/src/lib.rs:576) — the persistent agent checkout that DEV agents read diffs from, commit from, and which is surfaced in agent transcripts/QA evidence and copied/snapshotted. Before this change these secrets were transient per-process env args visible only during a single `up`; now every unconfigured app-driven deploy leaves a durable plaintext superuser password at rest inside a source tree — directly contradicting CXA-B017's stated goal ('no reader of source can predict a deployment's superuser password') for exactly the workloads CXA-B017 was hardening. Repro (static): deploy any unconfigured project once, then inspect codebase/.env — both keys present as literal text in the checkout dir. Suggested hardening: persist into a non-source state dir (e.g. project state/) or ensure .gitignore excludes .env upstream.

Running without .env or exported vars succeeds silently and interpolates empty secrets: COXAGENT_DB_DSN resolves to 'postgres://:@db:5432/coxagent' and Redis boots with --requirepass "" (empty password = unauthenticated Redis), which .env.example itself warns is 'a straight authentication bypass'. The new compose_security_gate test covers only cxa.yml; Rule 1 flags :-fallbacks but not bare ${VAR}, so this gap passes the gate. Fix should apply :? markers here too for consistency with CXA-B016.

tickets.title: CXA-B028 removes secret persistence but reintroduces CXA-B027's per-cycle secret rotation for unconfigured app-driven deploys
tickets.description: CXA-B027 (commit e4c819a) added materialize_deploy_secrets/upsert_dot_env to persist a generated PG_PASSWORD/COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD into the project-dir .env so they stay stable across deploy cycles — db locks POSTGRES_PASSWORD at empty-volume init, and without a write-back the DSN would drift from the volume's password on cycle 2, breaking DB auth and admin login. CXA-B028 (commit f5fbb09) removed persistence entirely (now resolve_deploy_secrets only seeds per-pass child-process env via seed_deploy_secrets; no std::env::set_var anywhere in crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs) and provides NO alternative cross-cycle mechanism. Repro: deploy an unconfigured project (no operator PG_PASSWORD/COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD in process env or .env) twice via DockerComposeDeploy::deploy on crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs:741. Cycle 1 generates random secret#1, Postgres volume initializes with it, DSN matches -> healthy. Cycle 2 calls resolve_deploy_secrets again which generates secret#2 because nothing was persisted, so coxagent's COXAGENT_DB_DSN uses #2 while the surviving db volume still holds #1 -> DB auth failure; COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD also rotates so root login fails. This is exactly the symptom CXA-B027 was filed to fix; B028 fixes the source-tree-cleartext half of the problem but discards cross-cycle stability instead of persisting outside the agent-managed source tree.

tickets.title: CXA-B030 shipped no code — per-cycle secret rotation for unconfigured app-driven deploys is still live (CXA-B027 regression)
tickets.description: The commit titled 'fix(CXA-B030)' (a27e1f0) adds only two doc files (docs/CXA-B004-config-initializer.md, docs/CXA-B006-release-pipeline.md) and changes zero production code, so the bug named in its own title remains unfixed. Reproduce: with no operator PG_PASSWORD/COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD set in process env or project-dir .env, call resolve_deploy_secrets() (crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs:78-87). It calls random_secret() freshly on EVERY deploy pass and nothing persists it anywhere (CXA-B028 removed the .env write-back; there is no cache/state-store/parent-env seed — confirmed by grep across crates). Deploy an app twice: cycle N seeds password A into docker compose subprocess; Postgres initializes pgdata (named volume, docker-compose.yml:45) with A; cycle N+1 regenerates password B and injects it into COXAGENT_DB_DSN=postgres://postgres:${PG_PASSWORD}...@db... (docker-compose.yml:35). Compose recreates both containers on env change, so the app now connects with B while Postgres still authenticates with A -> DB auth failure / broken admin login on every subsequent deploy of an unconfigured project. Expected per AC wording ('reintroduces ... per-cycle secret rotation'): stable secrets across cycles without writing them back into the source tree. Actual: fresh random secret each pass; DB/auth breaks from the second cycle onward.

tickets.title: CXA-B031 secret stability keyed to filesystem path; relocating an app-driven deploy regenerates credentials against initialized pgdata
tickets.description:
The new out-of-tree deploy-secret store keys each project's secrets by SHA-256 of its canonicalized work_dir absolute path (docker_compose.rs store_file(), line ~177). Postgres data however persists in docker NAMED volumes ('db:/var/lib/postgresql/data' in deploy/docker-compose.yml; 'source_cxa_data' in cxa.yml) which are independent of source location and persist across checkouts/moves. So an unconfigured app-driven deploy that runs from a different absolute path between cycles (agent slot relocated/re-cloned, or a fresh checkout) resolves a NEW generated PG_PASSWORD/COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD (different store file hash), yet reuses the already-initialized named pgdata volume -> Postgres rejects the new password and admin login breaks, silently resurrecting CXA-B027's auth-failure symptom under directory relocation. The stability test only covers one fixed temp dir reused across two calls, so it does not exercise this scenario.

Reproduce: 1) Deploy an unconfigured app from /tmp/proj-A (first cycle writes <HOME>/.local/share/coxagent/deploy-secrets/<hash-A>.env; pgdata volume initialised with that PG_PASSWORD). 2) Re-deploy the SAME logical app after moving/cloning it to /tmp/proj-B so compose_project_name stays equivalent but canonicalize() differs -> store_file yields <hash-B>.env, missing -> random_secret() generates a fresh password while postgres still authenticates with hash-A's value -> 'password authentication failed'. Confirmed root-cause by code inspection: store key = f(absolute workdir path) but DB state = f(docker named volume), two independent identity axes.

tickets.title: Persisted deploy secrets written world-readable (0644) despite code claiming chmod 0600
tickets.description: The in-flight CXA-B031 fix on this build writes generated superuser credentials (PG_PASSWORD / COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD) to ~/.coxagent-deploy/<proj>.secrets without ever setting file permissions. In crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs, persist_generated_deploy_secrets() (lines 240-279) contains two comments stating it restricts perms to owner-only ('chmod failure is not fatal', 'write then chmod 0600') but performs only std::fs::write(path, out) — there is NO set_permissions/PermissionsExt/chmod call anywhere in the function (grep for set_permissions|chmod|PermissionsExt|0o600 across the file finds only comments and an unrelated exec-bit check). REPRODUCE: cargo test -p coxagent-infrastructure deploy_secret_tests (writes store files), then 'stat -c %a ~/.coxagent-deploy/cox-t-cxa-b030-stable-*.secrets' -> returns 644; actual content holds live superuser password in plaintext. Expected: 600 so credentials at rest are not readable by other local users. Severity raised because these are live DB-superuser/admin credentials at rest and multi-user host exposure; note feat/CXA-B031 branch version calls set_secret_perms(), so this WIP regressed that hardening relative to its own sibling implementation.

tickets.title: Per-cycle secret rotation never shipped — fix exists only as divergent uncommitted WIP / unmerged branch

EVIDENCE: 'git show HEAD:crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs' lines 78-86 show resolve_deploy_secrets() mapping each missing key to a fresh random_secret() with no persistence/store; 'git merge-base --is-ancestor e4c819a/f5fbb09/6cf47d4 HEAD' returns NOT-in-current-branch for all of B027/B028/B031, and B030 added zero production code. The only corrections present are UNCOMMITTED working-tree edits on feat/CXA-B006 plus a separate unmerged feat/CXA-B031 branch that uses different naming/env vars (deploy_secret_store_path/COXAGENT_DEPLOY_SECRET_DIR vs store_file/deploy_secrets_root/COXAGENT_DEPLOY_SECRETS_DIR). tickets.title: CXA-B032 key-by-basename makes genuinely unrelated app-driven deploys share one secret store and docker volumes
tickets.description:
store_file() now keys each project's out-of-tree deploy-secret file solely by compose_project_name(work_dir), i.e. sanitized basenames 'cox-<parent>-<dir>' plus SHA(60)-char truncation (docker_compose.rs:185-193,390-403). Any two genuinely DISTINCT apps whose checkout parents+dirs share names resolve to ONE store file -> they read/write each other's PG_PASSWORD/COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD AND docker names their pgdata volumes identically (<project>_db), crossing credentials/data between unrelated deployments on one host/machine account.

Reproduce deterministically without docker:
1) mkdir -p /tmp/A/proj/repo && mkdir -p /tmp/B/proj2/repo
2) In crates/infrastructure, evaluate store_file() with those two absolute roots --- compose_project_name('/a/proj/repo') == compose_project_name('/b/proj2/repo') == 'cox-repo' => hasher input identical => IDENTICAL .env store filename.
3) Assertive repro already visible today: resolve_deploy_secrets_in(&'/a/proj/repo', root) then resolve_deploy_secrets_in(&'/b/proj2/repo', root) return EQUAL values instead of independent random secrets.
Contrast pre-fix guarantee recorded in this codebase ('canonicalised ... so ... two different projects never collide'). Note also container-port conflicts will arise when such colliding projects run simultaneously.
Actual(demonstrated by mirroring cpn logic above): equal keys/secrets and equal volume namespace.
Expected(CXA-B031 isolation contract preserved alongside B032 stability): distinct abs-path-projects keep separate stores while relocated clones still reuse theirs.

tickets.title: Changing store_file()'s hash input provides no migration from CXA-B031 path-keyed files -> first deploy after upgrade regenerates passwords against initialized pgdata

Any already-deployed unconfigured app that had its PG_PASSWORD stored under the OLD path-key will not find those values at its NEW name-key location on first post-upgrade cycle -> random_secret() generates fresh credentials while Postgres was already initialized with B031's value -> DB/admin auth failure reappears on exactly the affected deployments this ticket claims to stabilize.

tickets.title: Legacy world-readable deploy-secret store files are never remediated to 0600 once all required secrets are supplied externally
tickets.description: CXA-B033's fix chmods to 0600 only inside persist_generated_deploy_secrets -> restrict_store_to_owner. But resolve_deploy_secrets returns early at crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs:125-127 whenever missing_required_secrets() is empty (i.e. both PG_PASSWORD and COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD are provided via process env or project-dir .env). A <proj>.secrets file created at 0644 by a PRE-B033 build is therefore never re-permissioned once an operator fully configures those creds externally — live superuser credentials stay world-readable on disk indefinitely. Reproduce: create the off-repo store file manually at mode 0644 (echo 'PG_PASSWORD=x' 'COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=y' > $COXAGENT_DEPLOY_SECRET_DIR/<proj>.secrets; chmod 644), set PG_PASSWORD and COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD in process env, then call resolve_deploy_secrets(work_dir); observe returned vector is empty and stat -c %a on the .secrets file still reports 644 (confirmed empirically). Suggested fix: chmod/repair the existing store file unconditionally on each durable resolution pass before consulting it, not only inside persistence.

tickets.title: CXA-B036 migration silently bypassed whenever any value already exists in the NEW name-derived store
tickets.description:
adopt_legacy_cxb031_secrets returns early when stored (!stored.is_empty()) where stored was read from store_file() i.e. THE NAME-DERIVED FILE ONLY (docker_compose.rs:106-107,246-249). It never consults PATH-derived cxb031_store_file unless that new file is completely empty.

Repro timeline that defeats exactly what CXA-B036 promises ('first deploy after upgrade regenerates passwords'):
1) Deploy app under CXA-B031 -> PG_PASSWORD written to PATH-hash filename F(old); pgdata initialised with V.
2) Between CXA-B032 landing (~2h ago) and CXA-B036 landing today ANY single deploy cycle runs -> resolve reads empty name-file F(new), mints fresh random P != V into F(new) AND resolves from env so Postgres talks to volume initialised with V -> auth breaks.
3) Now install CXA-B036 on top -> next cycle reads F(new)=non-empty {PG_PASSWORD:P} -> adopt_legacy returns early -> correct V is never recovered even though F(old)==V still exists on disk.

The fix therefore recovers V only if NO write ever hit F(new) between the two releases - i.e., it depends on 'upgrade lands before any intervening cycle'. A regression test for exactly state 'F(new) non-empty wrong + F(old)==correct' would expose P!=V persistently.

Verified by reading docker_compose.rs lines 91-119 / 241-254 plus running coxagent_infrastructure binary filter 'deploy_secret': all green but none covers pre-populated-new-store.

tickets.title: Adopted superseded path-keyed secret files are never removed - duplicate live credentials linger indefinitely
tickets.description:
After adopt_legacy_cxb031_secrets copies value(s), write_stored_secrets persists ONLY to store_file()(name-derived). Nothing deletes/merges-reconciles cxb031_store_file(), so every upgraded project permanently retains an unreferenced second plaintext copy of its LIVE superuser password under its obsolete PATH-hash filename (~/.local/share/coxagent/deploy-secrets/<sha-of-old-path>.env), owner-only mode aside.

Across many apps hosted/deprecated/reserved-slots moved around one host these stale stores accumulate one-by-one forever - each holding active DB/admin credentials that rotate neither relation nor discoverability claim vs its twin - contradicting this repo's explicit minimal-cleartext-at-rest posture carried through CXA-B028/CXA-C016 decisions.

Repro/consequence observable purely statically from docker_compose.rs lines 106-117(copy loop)/241-254(read-only)/282(writes only store_file()); no runtime step needed beyond any successful first-post-upgrade resolution.

tickets.title: CXA-B039 turns legacy-store adoption into an indefinite override with no completion boundary — rotated secrets are permanently reverted
tickets.description: adopt_legacy_cxb031_secrets() now runs unconditionally on EVERY resolve_deploy_secrets_in() pass (the emptiness guard was removed at docker_compose.rs:263-276), but nothing ever deletes or expires cxb031_store_file after migration converges — grep confirms only repair_store_permissions() touches it (line 366, permission repair only). So once F(new)==F(old) converge they stay equal and reads are harmless; however if any legitimate future operation legitimately diverges F(new) from the stale legacy file (e.g. an admin remediating compromised credentials by deleting just the modern hash-named store to force regeneration), every subsequent cycle silently overwrites F(new)[k] back to the ancient V via line 272 'if stored.get(&k) != Some(&v)', permanently defeating rotation with no way to outvote except manually locating opaque hash-named files or wiping everything. REPRO: stage converged state {PG=V} in both store_file and cxb031_store_file for one work_dir under a shared COXAGENT_DEPLOY_SECRETS_DIR; delete ONLY store_file; call resolve_deploy_secrets_in -> adopt reads cxb031_store_file V != absent -> reinserts V, so regenerated R never survives even one pass, contradicting any secret-rotation workflow this ticket family is meant to stabilise. Impact: unconfigured-app superuser credentials can be permanently pinned to stale values / reused indefinitely after compromise.

tickets.title: Legacy adoption can drag ANOTHER project's credentials when its canonical path is reused by a differently-named compose project
tickets.description: Because CXA-B039 removed the early bail-out but kept ownership tied ONLY to 'same canonicalized absolute path' (docker_compose.rs:268-275) with NO check that compose_project_name matches, a fresh checkout of an unrelated/different app placed into a directory where some earlier B031-era app left its path-keyed store file will adopt THAT other app's PG_PASSWORD/ADMIN creds as its own on first unconfigured deploy even though their pgdata volumes (<own_compose_name>_db) differ. If that new volume is already initialized elsewhere, seeding wrong creds resurrects exactly the DB/admin auth failure this family exists to prevent — now caused BY migration rather than fixed by it. Two genuinely distinct apps need only share one directory over time plus one secret_root (~/.local/share/coxagent/deploy-secrets); with per-slot worktrees they normally don't collide because names differ per slot and volumes initialize fresh-consistent each cycle, so real-world probability is low unless directories get repurposed across apps.

tickets.title: CXA-B042 expiry deletes the legacy store BEFORE the modern store is persisted, risking simultaneous loss of both on a best-effort persist failure
tickets.description: In adopt_legacy_cxb031_secrets (crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs:267-296), after copying legacy values into the in-memory `stored` map, `expire_legacy_store()` removes cxb031_store_file(F(old)) right away. Because the preceding loop guarantees stored[k]==v for every key k present in F(old), the guard `!legacy.is_empty() && legacy.iter().all(...)` is always true whenever F(old) is non-empty — so F(old) is deleted unconditionally on this very pass, BEFORE resolve_deploy_secrets_in calls write_stored_secrets(store_file=...F(new)) at line 125. The doc comment claims 'Its content lives on inside modern ([store_file]), which adoption copied into before this runs' — but adoption only mutates a HashMap; nothing is written to F(new) until later. write_stored_secrets (lines 324-358) is best-effort and silently swallows create_dir_all/write/rename failures. Repro (static trace): any run where missing secrets are non-empty, an old-format F(old) file exists with a required key, and persisting to F(new) fails (e.g. disk full / permissions changed / rename fails mid-window), or where the process crashes between line 286 and line 125 -> both stores are gone; next cycle regenerates random secrets against already-initialized pgdata -> Postgres admin/DB auth failure, exactly the CXA-B036/B039 regression class this whole chain was fixing. The delete should be moved AFTER write_stored_secrets succeeds so convergence expiry can never outrun persistence.

design_system.principles: Opinionated, minimal token system applied consistently: one base unit (2px), one font, one accent. Color contrast always tested against the nearest surface; no color alone carries meaning. Dark-first palette scales light theme by remapping each variable, not inventing new ones. Inter is the sole typeface — scale and weight do the work, never variable fonts. Every interactive element has a 0.15s transition; no instant state changes. 8px is the rhythm: spacing, radius, and sizing follow multiples of 8. Zero decorative gradients except where brand identity demands it (app mark).
design_system.typography: Inter for all text — base 14px, line-height 1.55. Scale: xs 10px/weight-700, sm 12px/weight-600, base 14px/weight-400, md 15px/weight-500, lg 18px/weight-600, xl 22px/weight-800. Monospace: ui-monospace,Menlo for all code, file paths, identifiers, and data labels at 11.5px. Letter-spacing: 0 for body, +0.6px for uppercase micro-labels, -0.4px for display titles.
components: app-mark: 34×34px square, 10px radius, vertical gradient brand (#22D3EE to #0E7490), white icon, no stroke
cards: 14px radius (via --r), 1px solid border-default, card background, hover border to border-default
chips: 20px pill radius, card background, 1px border-default, 7×14px padding, 12.5px font-weight-600
buttons-primary: 8px radius, filled primary bg, white text, 8×16px padding, 12.5px weight-600, border-less
buttons-ghost: 9px radius, card-elevated bg, 1px border-default, 8×13px padding, text-secondary
buttons-destructive: 9px radius, transparent bg, 1px border-default, hover: red border + red 7% tint bg
inputs: 8px radius, card-elevated bg, 1px border-default, 9×11px padding, focus: solidify accent border
nav-items: 10px radius, transparent bg, hover: 6% tint on text-color, active: accent 14% tint bg
avatars: 50% circular, 40px diameter, gradient bg (primary→primary-focus-ring), bold initial, 14px text
badges: 20px pill, 2×8px padding, 10px weight-700, uppercase +0.4px tracking, tinted bg matching semantic color
modals: 14px radius, 1px border-default, card-bg, box-shadow 0 24px 70px rgba(0,0,0,0.5), 5–9px border radius for inner elements
dropdowns-popovers: 11–14px radius, 1px border-default, card-bg, box-shadow 0 12–50px rgba(0,0,0,0.32–0.45), 5–8px padding
toasts: 10px radius, left 3px accent-colored border, card-bg, box-shadow 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.35), 11px radius for inner elements
chat-bubbles-outgoing: 12px 4px 12px 12px radius, accent filled bg, transparent border, white text
status-dot: 7×7px circle, muted color by default, primary-white when active, 2px panel border shadow when overlaid on avatars
empty-states: center-aligned, icon 34px at 0.7 opacity with accent color, 15px weight-600 subtitle in muted-color, 12.5px tertiary helper text below

docs.title: Editable Prompt System with Per-Project Override
docs.body:
# Editable Prompt System with Per-Project Override

**Keywords:** prompts, system prompt, ceremony, per-project override, prompts/*.md, role sections, user story format, language directive

## Overview

The Editable Prompt System defines the role-based system prompts (PO, SM, BA, SA, PD, DEV) and a composer that assembles the final system prompt from base invariants plus a per-role section. It is the mechanism by which every ceremony/task decision is framed in a consistent voice and format for the agent.

The **per-project override** capability — letting a workspace override these prompts from `prompts/*.md` — is **declared but not yet implemented**. The module docstring (`crates/application/src/prompts.rs:1-3`) states it as "a later milestone." As of now all 75+ call sites use the embedded constants directly; there is no disk loading of prompt text anywhere in the codebase.

## How it works

All prompt text lives as embedded constants in `crates/application/src/prompts.rs`. Each role has a section constant (`PO`, `SM`, `BA`, `SA`, `PD`, `DEV`); shared invariants are in `PROCESS_INVARIANTS` and `ENGINEERING_STANDARDS`. These are composed into a single system prompt by the function:

```rust
system_prompt(role_section: &str) -> String
```

which wraps an injected engine style + session context preamble around the base rules (`BASE`) and the given role section.

Callers select their role's prompt via a one-line selector such as:

```rust
let sp = system_prompt(prompts::DEV);
```

Every decision path — dev tasks (`work.rs`), analysis tasks (`analysis.rs`), PO/SM/BA/SA ceremonies — calls this composer with its own role constant. There is no lookup of overrides at any call site; each simply references the compile-time constant.

The intended (future) seam for per-project overrides would be between "caller picks a role" and "composer reads text": instead of always using the embedded constant string, resolve it from workspace-supplied markdown first. That seam does not exist yet.

## Usage

There is no user-facing surface yet — this is internal-only plumbing consumed by task dispatch. From an agent/runtime perspective there is nothing to configure or invoke directly:

```text
# (planned) place override files in a managed workspace:
workspace/
  prompts/
    PO.md        # optional override
    SM.md        # optional override
    ...

# behavior today: none of these files are read.
```

The only knob that affects prompt *content* today flows through configuration (see Configuration): setting `language` changes reply phrasing directives inside composed prompts.

## Interface

### Functions/types (Rust)

| Name | Signature / note |
|------|------------------|
| `system_prompt(role_section)` | Composer; returns full rendered system-prompt string |
| Base constants | Struct(s)/consts holding shared rules |
| Role constants | Const strings: one per ceremony role |

### Selector pattern at call sites

Each dispatch path names its own section explicitly:

```rust
use crate::prompts;
let sp = system_prompt(prompts::DEV);      // dev task briefings
let sp = system_prompt(prompts::ANALYSIS); // analysis tasks
// ...one per PO/SM/BA/SA ceremony path
```

There are **no** endpoints or CLI flags; prompting happens entirely inside application-layer task construction.

## Configuration

Settings that change what appears inside prompts:

- **`language`** (`Language`, config.rs ~161) — adds a reply-directive sentence to composed prompts so responses come back in the target language.
- **`token_compress`** (config.rs ~221) — when enabled compresses/shortens embedded prompt text before injection (default behavior applies when off).

These affect *content* indirectly. There is currently **no** setting controlling an override directory or editable-prompt source because that feature does not exist yet.

*(Note: config also has engine/model-per-role settings labeled "per_role" — those govern which model serves each role and are unrelated to editable prompt text.)*

## Edge cases and limits

- **No overrides exist.** Writing files under a workspace `prompts/` directory has zero effect today — nothing reads them. This is deliberate (declared milestone), but surprising if you assume otherwise.
- **All changes require recompilation.** Because sections are embedded consts, editing prompt copy means editing Rust source and rebuilding.
- Prompts are kept intentionally short because behavioral state rules live in code rather than prose — do not expect exhaustive instructions inside any single section.
- The composer takes exactly one role section; there is no facility to stack arbitrary additional sections at runtime.

## Code map

- `crates/application/src/prompts.rs` — all embedded default sections (`BASE`, shared invariants, engineering standards) plus individual ceremony roles; home of the future milestone comment at lines 1–3.
- Call sites (each uses `system_prompt(prompts::X)`): dev task briefing (`work.rs`), analysis briefing (`analysis.rs`)**, and one per PO/SM/BA/SA ceremony path across application-layer task construction.

> Path details above reflect current repository layout; verify exact filenames before relying on them for edits since this module was recently split along its seams.

## Related

- Task-dispatch/task-runner pages that consume these prompts.
- Any page covering config settings **per project / per workspace**, where an override directory would eventually be exposed.
