# Editable Prompt System with Per-Project Override

**Keywords:** prompts, system prompt, ceremony, per-project override, prompts/*.md, role sections, engineering standards, token_saver, language directive

## Overview

The Editable Prompt System defines the role-based system prompts (PO, SM, BA, SA, PD, DEV) and a composer that assembles the final system prompt from base invariants plus a per-role section. It is the mechanism by which every ceremony/task decision is framed in a consistent voice and format for the agent.

The **per-project override** capability — letting a workspace override these prompts from `prompts/*.md` — is **declared but not yet implemented**. The module docstring (`crates/application/src/prompts.rs:1-4`) states it as "a later milestone." As of now all ~40 call sites use the embedded constants directly; there is no disk loading of prompt text anywhere in the codebase.

## How it works

All prompt text lives as embedded constants in `crates/application/src/prompts.rs`. Each role has a section constant (`PO`, `SM`, `BA`, `SA`, `PD`, `DEV`); shared rules live in three constants: `BASE` (the practitioner preamble), `PROCESS_INVARIANTS` (orchestrator-enforced process law), and `ENGINEERING_STANDARDS` (house rules baked into every prompt). These are composed into a single system prompt by:

```rust
// crates/application/src/prompts.rs:357
pub fn system_prompt(role_section: &str) -> String {
    format!("{BASE}\n\n{ENGINEERING_STANDARDS}\n\n{role_section}")
}
```

Note that `PROCESS_INVARIANTS` and any engine-style/session-context preamble are handled outside this composer at dispatch time; this function always renders exactly three blank-line-separated sections: BASE → ENGINEERING_STANDARDS → role section.

Callers select their role's prompt via one-line selectors such as:

```rust
let sp = crate::prompts::system_prompt(crate::prompts::DEV);
```

Every decision path — dev tasks (`use_cases/run_dev/**`), analysis (`run_sa.rs`), reviews (`run_reviews.rs`), PO/SM/BA/SA ceremonies (`run_ba.rs`, `scrum.rs`, etc.) — calls this composer with its own role constant. Many call sites additionally append runtime context blocks returned by two helpers defined here:

- **`repo_map_block(files_port, work_dir, enabled)`** — appends a `.coxagent/REPO_MAP.md` compact slice so code-touching agents locate files without re-scanning; empty when disabled or no map exists.
- **`focus_block(files_port, work_dir, query)`** — appends a ticket-scoped slice of the code graph (top symbols/files plus callers) so DEV/SA jump straight to relevant code.

The intended (future) seam for per-project overrides would be between "caller picks a role" and "composer reads text": instead of always using the embedded constant string, resolve it from workspace-supplied markdown first. That seam does not exist yet.

## Usage

There is no user-facing surface yet — this is internal-only plumbing consumed by task dispatch. From an agent/runtime perspective there is nothing to configure or invoke directly:

```text
# (planned) place override files in a managed workspace:
workspace/
  prompts/
    PO.md        # optional override
    SM.md        # optional override
    ...

# behavior today: none of these files are read.
```

The only knobs that affect prompt *content* today flow through configuration (see Configuration): setting `language` changes reply phrasing directives inside composed prompts; enabling token saving changes whether repo-map/focus context blocks are appended.

## Interface

### Functions/types (Rust)

| Name | Signature / note |
|------|------------------|
| `system_prompt(role_section)` | Composer at prompts.rs:357; renders exactly `BASE\n\nENGINEERING_STANDARDS\n\n{role}` |
| `repo_map_block(files?, work_dir, enabled)` | Returns compact repo-map context block or empty string |
| `focus_block(files?, work_dir, query)` | Returns ticket-scoped code-graph context block or empty string |
| Base constants | ``BASE`` / ``PROCESS_INVARIANTS`` / ``ENGINEERING_STANDARDS`` — shared rules |
| Role constants | ``PO`` / ``SM`` / ``BA`` / ``SA`` / ``PD`` / ``DEV`` plus derived ``TEST`` / ``DOCS`` / ``DEV_HEAL`` / ``DESIGN_SYSTEM`` |

### Selector pattern at call sites

Each dispatch path names its own section explicitly:

```rust
use crate::prompts;
let sp = crate::prompts::system_prompt(crate::prompts::DEV);      // dev briefings (use_cases/run_dev)
let sp = crate::prompts::system_prompt(crate::prompts::SA);       // analysis/review paths
let sp = crate::prompts::system_prompt(crate::prompts::BA);       // grooming/scrum paths
// ...one per PO/SM ceremony path across use_cases/*
```

There are **no** endpoints or CLI flags; prompting happens entirely inside application-layer task construction.

## Configuration

Settings that change what appears inside composed prompts:

- **`language`** (`Language`, config.rs:154) — default `En`. When set to another value (e.g. Vietnamese), its repr directive (`Language.reply_directive()`) is appended to ceremony prompts so responses come back in that language while keeping technical labels intact.
- **`token_saver`** (bool, config.rs:224) — when enabled appends optional compact context blocks (`repo_map_block`, sometimes with history trimming) to prompts instead of full context; gates whether run_reviews/run_chat_reply attach repo-map slices. Default true in test fixtures; see config defaults for production.

These affect *content* indirectly. There is currently **no** setting controlling an override directory or editable-prompt source because that feature does not exist yet.

*(Note: config also has engine/model-per-role settings labeled "per_role" — those govern which model serves each role and are unrelated to editable prompt text.)*

## Edge cases and limits

- **No overrides exist.** Writing files under a workspace `prompts/` directory has zero effect today — nothing reads them. This is deliberate (declared milestone), but surprising if you assume otherwise.
- **All changes require recompilation.** Because sections are embedded consts at compile time in Rust source only.
- Prompts are kept intentionally short because behavioral state rules live in code rather than prose.
- The composer takes exactly one role section plus BASE + ENGINEERING_STANDARDS; there is no facility to stack arbitrary additional sections at runtime beyond the optional repo-map/focus blocks appended at call sites.
- A regression guard added under CXA-F022 locks this composition invariant on purpose: do not drop/reorder/inline ENGINEERING_STANDARDS into BASE without breaking tests that assert BASE opens first and the standards sit between BASE and every role section.

docs.title: Architecture Review
docs.body:
🏛️ **Architecture review — after sprint 112** · **Risk: HIGH**

**Architecture & layering:** Clean/hexagonal layering is real and enforced: domain (crates/domain) imports only std/serde/time/semver, application exposes ports in crates/application/src/ports/outbound/{git,state_store,audit,deploy,...}.rs and keeps decisions pure, infrastructure implements adapters (sql_store.rs, json_store.rs, redis_coord.rs), presentation is a thin axum router. hexagonal_gate.rs compiles an empty GRANDFATHERED list so no application file does direct IO. However the layering leaks: crates/presentation/src/server/mod.rs:973 run_cli() shells out via tokio::process inline and hosts a ~200-route flat registry with chat/business logic, and heavy tree-sitter parsing grammars are compiled into the application crate rather than an infrastructure adapter — presentation is not thin.
**Persistence / DB:** Real multi-store: Postgres via tokio-postgres+deadpool-postgres for state (sql_store.rs single JSONB row per project + revision CAS) and auth (sql_auth.rs users/tokens/sessions); Redis (redis 0.27) for ephemeral leases/sessions/pubsub; a JSON-file store (json_store.rs) as default + best-effort mirror of Postgres; MongoDB via docs_store.rs for user docs. No migration tool — schemas are idempotent INIT_SQL with 'ALTER ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS' run on connect (sql_auth.rs:27-52), which makes schema evolution ad-hoc and risky.
**Caching:** In-memory session cache with per-request hydration from Redis/PG in sql_auth.rs hydrate_session(); Redis doubles as fast-path coord TTL keys. No general read cache: each API call re-loads the whole project JSONB row per project (server/mod.rs doc_list/store.load), so nothing else is cached.
**Concurrency & consistency:** Solid foundations: optimistic concurrency via revision CAS with PortError::Conflict (sql_store persist_at_revision), transactional claim_ticket under SELECT FOR UPDATE row lock, advisory file lock for JSON store atomic_write+rename, Redis-native-TTL leases. Races are deliberately avoided with write-lock-first channel lookups.
**Scalability & performance:** A modular monolith compiled into four thin service binaries that all share one codebase and serve different routes based on COXAGENT_ROLE (gateway/realtime/knowledge). All projects are held in-memory in AppState HashMap; single Postgres row per project serializes all its writes; SSE loop pushes every second per connection. Ready for modest N instances but per-project row = bottleneck at scale.
**Reliability & resilience:** Local JSON mirror of Postgres plus rolling backups give DR/reseed paths; health endpoint + compose healthcheck exist. But rest_store has only a single 120s timeout with no retry/idempotency beyond 409-conflict handling; operator acquire_operator returns Ok(true) when no Redis even in cluster mode; no circuit breakers on external CLIs/forges.
**Security:** Good hygiene overall: argon2 password hashing, TOTP 2FA enrollment/verify, HttpOnly cookies + CSP/X-Frame headers + auth rate limiting in middleware/, committed_secrets_gate proves a real leaked admin password was found & fixed. Critical gap: /api/projects/:pid/store store_rpc_ep is NOT behind resolve_principal — handoff marks P5a auth enforcement as not applied — so when auth is enabled any anonymous caller can load or overwrite full project state through this write surface.
**Observability:** Weakest area: only tracing to stderr/logs via init_tracing(); metrics in metrics.go/metrics.rs are pure domain stats exposed through UI endpoints but there is NO Prometheus/OpenTelemetry exporter or /metrics endpoint anywhere in crates/services — nothing to drive alerting or dashboards for operations.
**API & integration:** Single large flat route table (~200 routes) built inline in serve_full() inside server/mod.rs making contracts hard to version or review atomically; OpenAPI 3.1 document exists (/api/openapi backed by openpi::document() plus an openapi_gate test). Error mapping exists on store RPC but general handlers mix ad-hoc status codes.
**Testability & quality:** Strong discipline unmatched by typical repos: hexagonal_gate dead-code/no-IO ratchet with shrinking grandfather list, committed_secrets_gate scanning tracked files without embedding secrets, clippy_baseline_ratchet warnings=deny pedantic baseline, openapi_gate/docs_ports gate tests plus Playwright e2e with golden screenshots over web/js*. Test coverage of critical paths appears thorough.
**Cost & tech choices:** Deliberately self-contained/vendored assets avoid CDN/lock-in costs, but running PG+Redis+MongoDB simultaneously raises operational/licensing burden relative to the value added by Mongo docs vs simple state storage; tree-sitter bundled grammars bloat binary size/build time across many language grammars loaded into the application layer.
**Verdict:** Architecture bones are strong (clean ports/pure domain/enforced IO ratchet) but three long-term risks undermine it if left unchecked while features keep landing: an unauthenticated write surface on /store contradicts the otherwise-good RBAC model; observability cannot support operation at scale; and AGENTS.md claims 'no oversized files' while ~29 production sources exceed 500 lines.

docs.title: Test Coverage Gap Detection
docs.body:
The original page cited `crates/application/src/use_cases/coverage.rs` (doesn't exist) and `run_dev/gates.rs` (incomplete path). I need to find the real implementation. Let me read the candidate files.Now I understand the real feature — it's the DoD gate that detects production-code changes shipping without test changes. Let me find the callers and the gate enforcement.Let me read the port definition, the adapter, and the `working_tree()` helper to nail down the exact types.Let me verify how the gate failure is escalated (merge_policy) and confirm `DevMode`/`record_failure_at`/`run_tests_scoped` identifiers.I now have a fully verified picture. The feature is the regression-test DoD gate: a bug fix that touches production code but no tests gets one repair pass, then a `FailureLayer::Gate`/`"regression-test"` failure. The real files are in `run_dev/gates.rs` + `run_dev/mod.rs`, not `coverage.rs`. Writing the complete corrected page:

FOLDER: -
# Test Coverage Gap Detection

**Keywords:** regression test gate, DoD, working tree diff, bug fix, coverage gap, `diff_touches_tests`, `WorkingTreeDiff`, `FailureLayer::Gate`, repair pass, definition of done

## Overview
A mechanical Definition-of-Done gate that refuses to let a bug fix ship on faith. After the dev engine finishes a fix, the working tree is snapshotted once through `GitPort::working_tree`; if a `DevMode::Bug` pass changed production code without changing anything test-shaped, the gate issues one bounded repair pass to add a regression test, then re-checks. A fix that still carries no test — or whose new test leaves the suite red — is recorded as a `FailureLayer::Gate` failure and returned to the queue. It is structural ("did a test-shaped change land"), not line/branch coverage.

## How it works
The gate lives in `RunDevUseCase::execute` (`crates/application/src/use_cases/run_dev/mod.rs`), at the tail of a bug-fix pass, after the suite has already gone green:

1. **One snapshot.** `self.working_tree()` (`run_dev/mod.rs:120`) calls `GitPort::working_tree` and unwraps to `WorkingTreeDiff::default()` on error or when `self.git` is `None`. The adapter `SystemGit::working_tree` (`infrastructure/src/git/system_git.rs:67`) makes three git reads — `diff HEAD --name-only`, `ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, `diff HEAD`, `diff HEAD -U0` — plus a filesystem scan for each changed file's first `#[cfg(test)]` line, and packs them into one `WorkingTreeDiff` so every gate reads the same snapshot.
2. **The trigger** (`run_dev/mod.rs:755`):
   ```rust
   if self.mode == DevMode::Bug
       && !gates::diff_is_docs_only(&tree)
       && !gates::diff_touches_tests(&tree)
   ```
   Bug fix, not docs-only, touches no test → gap detected.
3. **Repair pass.** The engine is resumed (`engine.resume_run(sid, &fixup, ...)`) or, with no session, a fresh `AgentRequest` is run (`engine.run(repair)`), both with a 900 s timeout. The `fixup` prompt tells the agent exactly where the gate looks for tests.
4. **Re-check on a fresh snapshot** (`run_dev/mod.rs:782`): `if !gates::diff_touches_tests(&self.working_tree().await)`. Still no test → `record_failure_at(&id, "bug fix shipped without a regression test", FailureLayer::Gate, "regression-test", Vec::new())` (`run_dev/failures.rs:26`), claim released, `Err` returned.
5. **Suite still green.** If a test was added, `deploy.run_tests_scoped(&self.work_dir, &changed)` re-runs the scoped suite. Red → `record_failure_at(..., "regression test added but suite is red", FailureLayer::Gate, "tests", ...)`, `Err` returned.
6. **Escalation.** The recorded `FailureLayer::Gate` failures feed `merge_policy::route_from_failures` (`merge_policy.rs:151`): when every real attempt died on a gate, the route is `EscalationRoute::Mechanical` — a repair brief to the SA, not a redesign of something that was never wrong.

The detection itself is pure: `gates.rs` are plain functions over `WorkingTreeDiff`, testable with a struct literal (the comment at the top of `gates.rs` explains this is why the IO was pushed out to the port).

## Usage
No user-facing API — the gate fires inside the autonomous dev cycle (`RunCycleUseCase` calls `self.dev(DevMode::Bug).execute()`, `cycle/mod.rs:744`). What an operator or agent observes:

The repair prompt the dev engine receives:
```text
Your fix for CX-42 ships with NO regression test. Add a test that FAILS
without your fix and passes with it — that is the only proof the bug is
dead. Put it where the gate can see it: a `tests/` path, a `*_test.rs` /
`*.test.ts` file, or an added `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]`/`it(`/`def test_`
block. Do not start new work or commit.
```

If the repair pass still adds nothing test-shaped, the ticket is returned to the queue with a structured failure (visible in state/activity):
```text
why:   "bug fix shipped without a regression test"
layer: FailureLayer::Gate
gate:  "regression-test"
err:   "Bug fix for CX-42 has no regression test — returned to the queue"
```
If the repair adds a test but the suite goes red:
```text
why:   "regression test added but suite is red"
layer: FailureLayer::Gate
gate:  "tests"
err:   "Bug fix regression test left suite red on CX-42"
```

Where the gate "sees" a test (any one is enough): a path containing `tests/`, starting with `tests/`, ending in `_test.rs` / `_test.go` / `.test.ts` / `.test.js`, or containing `test_`; OR an added diff line carrying `#[test]`, `#[tokio::test]`, `def test_`, `it(`, or `func Test`; OR an edited line that falls at or below its file's first `#[cfg(test)]` marker.

## Interface
Pure detection functions in `crates/application/src/use_cases/run_dev/gates.rs` (all `#[must_use]`, all take `&WorkingTreeDiff`):
- `diff_touches_tests(tree: &WorkingTreeDiff) -> bool` — the main detector; OR of path-shape, added-marker, and inline-test-module checks.
- `diff_touches_inline_test_module(tree: &WorkingTreeDiff) -> bool` — private; parses `unified0_diff` hunk headers `@@ -a,b +c,d @@`, takes new-side start `c`, returns true when `c > cfg_test_line[file]`.
- `diff_is_docs_only(tree: &WorkingTreeDiff) -> bool` — exempts docs/assets/licence/gitignore-only changes.
- `build_relevant(changed: &[String]) -> Vec<String>` — strips `BUILD_IRRELEVANT` paths before scoping.
- `lints_touch_changed_files(tree: &WorkingTreeDiff, lint_files: &[String]) -> bool` — co-resident lint-attribution helper (not part of the coverage gate, but same snapshot).

Snapshot type `WorkingTreeDiff` (`crates/application/src/ports/outbound/git.rs:22`):
- `changed_paths: Vec<String>` — tracked-vs-HEAD plus untracked, repo-relative.
- `full_diff: String` — `git diff HEAD`.
- `unified0_diff: String` — `git diff HEAD -U0` (no context; line numbers are the changed lines).
- `cfg_test_line: BTreeMap<String, usize>` — 0-based line of each changed file's first `#[cfg(test)]`.

Port: `GitPort::working_tree(&self, work_dir: &Path) -> Result<WorkingTreeDiff, PortError>` (`ports/outbound/git.rs:65`); default returns an empty tree (so a test double that ignores it reads as "nothing changed"). Adapter: `SystemGit::working_tree` (`infrastructure/src/git/system_git.rs:67`).

Trigger selector: `DevMode::Bug` (`run_dev/mod.rs:24`). The gate is gated on `self.mode == DevMode::Bug`; `DevMode::Feature` passes do not run it.

## Configuration
No runtime settings — the gate is hardcoded policy. The knobs that exist are constants in `gates.rs` and `run_dev/mod.rs`:
- **Scope:** `DevMode::Bug` only. Feature work is exempt by design.
- **Docs-only exemption** (`diff_is_docs_only`): extensions `.md .txt .adoc .rst .png .jpg .jpeg .svg .gif`; names ending `license` or `.gitignore`; paths under `docs/` or containing `/docs/`. Any non-matching file breaks the exemption.
- **`BUILD_IRRELEVANT`** (`gates.rs:135`): `.claude/`, `.gitnexus/`, `backups/`, `node_modules/`, `target/`, `cox-opencode.json`, `cox-config.json`, `.DS_Store`. Used by `build_relevant` to scope tests and to keep scratch from masquerading as a build change.
- **Repair-pass timeout:** `Duration::from_secs(900)` (15 min) for both `resume_run` and the fresh `AgentRequest`.
- **Test-shape markers:** path substrings `tests/`, `_test.rs`, `_test.go`, `.test.ts`, `.test.js`, `test_`; added-line markers `#[test]`, `#[tokio::test]`, `def test_`, `it(`, `func Test`.
- **Failure classification:** `FailureLayer::Gate`, gate string `"regression-test"` (no test) or `"tests"` (suite red). These strings are matched by `merge_policy::escalation_route`'s `gates` list (`"regression test"`, `"suite is red"`, `"left tests red"`).

## Edge cases and limits
- **Features are exempt.** Only `DevMode::Bug` runs the gate; a feature that ships without tests is not caught here.
- **Structural, not coverage.** It checks that a test-shaped change landed, not that the changed lines are exercised. A test in the right file that never calls the fixed code passes the gate.
- **Git-less projects read as empty.** With `self.git == None` (or any adapter error), `working_tree()` returns `WorkingTreeDiff::default()`: `diff_touches_tests` is false and `diff_is_docs_only` is false, so the gate fires for every bug fix even when nothing changed. Projects without git should not wire `DevMode::Bug` against this gate, or should provide a `GitPort` adapter.
- **Inline-test detection is Rust-specific.** `diff_touches_inline_test_module` keys off `#[cfg(test)]`; other languages rely on path-shape or added markers. The comment at `gates.rs:82` calls out that this exists precisely because a Rust fix inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` adds no `#[test]` line and sits in no test-shaped path.
- **One repair pass, then hard fail.** The gate does not loop; a second miss is a `Gate` failure returned to the queue. Repeated gate-only failures escalate as `EscalationRoute::Mechanical` (repair), not `Design` (redesign).
- **Suite must stay green with the new test.** Adding a test that breaks the suite is the `"tests"` failure, not a pass.
- **Snapshot consistency is deliberate.** The adapter takes all reads together; a path list from one moment and a diff from another is how a gate mis-blames a change (see the comment at `system_git.rs:71`).
- **Does not file a bug ticket itself** for the gap — unlike `file_test_failure` (`qa_evidence.rs:14`), which files a High bug when the suite is red. This gate records an attempt failure and returns the ticket to the queue.

## Code map
- `crates/application/src/use_cases/run_dev/gates.rs` — the pure detection functions over `WorkingTreeDiff`: `diff_touches_tests`, `diff_touches_inline_test_module`, `diff_is_docs_only`, `build_relevant`, `lints_touch_changed_files`, plus their unit tests (`test_paths_and_added_markers_count_as_tests`, `editing_an_existing_inline_test_counts_changing_production_does_not`, `docs_only_spares_readme_fixes_but_not_code`, `agent_scratch_never_counts_as_a_build_change`).
- `crates/application/src/use_cases/run_dev/mod.rs` — gate enforcement in `RunDevUseCase::execute` (the `DevMode::Bug && !diff_is_docs_only && !diff_touches_tests` block at line 751, the repair pass, the re-check at line 782, the scoped-suite re-run at line 799); the `working_tree()` snapshot helper at line 120; the `DevMode` enum at line 24.
- `crates/application/src/use_cases/run_dev/failures.rs` — `RunDevUseCase::record_failure_at`, which writes the `FailureLayer::Gate` / `"regression-test"` (or `"tests"`) attempt failure the merge policy later reads.
- `crates/application/src/ports/outbound/git.rs` — the `WorkingTreeDiff` struct (line 22) and the `GitPort::working_tree` port method (line 65) the gate reads through.
- `crates/infrastructure/src/git/system_git.rs` — `SystemGit::working_tree` (line 67), the one adapter that shells out to git and the filesystem to build the snapshot (tracked + untracked paths, full diff, `-U0` diff, `cfg_test_line` map).
- `crates/application/src/ports/outbound/deploy.rs` — `DeployPort::run_tests_scoped` (line 195), used to re-run the scoped suite after the repair pass adds a test.
- `crates/application/src/use_cases/merge_policy.rs` — `route_from_failures` (line 151) and `escalation_route` (line 176), which turn `FailureLayer::Gate`-only histories into `EscalationRoute::Mechanical` (repair, not redesign).
- `crates/application/src/state/work.rs` — `AttemptFailure` and `FailureLayer::Gate` (line 140), the recorded shape of a gate failure.
- `crates/application/src/use_cases/cycle/qa_evidence.rs` — distinct but adjacent: `file_test_failure` (line 14) files a High bug when the suite is red, and `test_has_work` (line 283) decides whether the TEST role has anything to verify. Not part of this gate, but the other quality signals an agent will land on when reading the DoD area.

## Related
- **Definition of Done / dev-cycle gates** — the broader DoD surface (lint attribution, scoped test scoping, green-suite requirement) that this gate is one part of; the same `WorkingTreeDiff` snapshot feeds `build_relevant` (test scoping) and `lints_touch_changed_files` in the same `execute` pass.
- **Merge policy / escalation** — `crates/application/src/use_cases/merge_policy.rs`; how repeated gate failures route to `EscalationRoute::Mechanical` instead of a redesign.
- **Verify cache** — `crates/application/src/verify_cache.rs`; the green-tree fingerprint recorded at `run_dev/mod.rs:822` once all gates (this one included) pass.
- **Architecture rule (hexagonal gate)** — `crates/app/tests/hexagonal_gate.rs` and the note in `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: `GitPort::working_tree` → `run_dev/gates.rs` is the canonical "adapter takes the snapshot, decision is a pure function" pattern this gate follows.

So the page's central claim ("this file was hardened to required-variable syntax, commit 7247e21") is TRUE historically but describes a state **not present in the current code**. The ticket itself confirms: "uses non-required ${PG_USER}/${PG_PASSWORD}/${REDIS_PASSWORD} -> silent blank credentials when .env absent."

The page needs to be corrected to describe the ACTUAL current state: plain `${VAR}` with silent blank credentials. This is precisely what the ticket is about — a pending bug, not a fixed one.

I have all the evidence I need. The key finding:

FOLDER: -
# docker-compose.cxa.yml (standalone CXA backend)

**Keywords:** docker compose, PG_USER, PG_PASSWORD, REDIS_PASSWORD, blank credential, silent fallback, ${VAR}, cxa-backend, coxagent_db, postgres 5433, redis 6379

## Overview

`deploy/docker-compose.cxa.yml` brings up Postgres + Redis for the native CXA hub on a single host as its own compose project (`cxa-backend`), so it does not collide with the web app or the split deploy. It is for an operator running only CXA's backing store. **As committed on this branch it interpolates all three secrets with non-required `${VAR}` syntax — composing without `.env` silently starts Postgres/Redis with blank credentials.** A fix hardening these to required `${VAR?...}` exists only on feature branches and has not landed.

## How it works

Compose resolves environment interpolation at parse time. This file uses **non-required** `${VAR}` for every secret — if `PG_USER`, `PG_PASSWORD`, or `REDIS_PASSWORD` is unset in `.env`, compose substitutes an empty string and proceeds to start the containers rather than aborting (`POSTGRES_USER: ${PG_USER}`, `--requirepass "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"`). That is the vulnerability this ticket tracks.

The two services:

- **db** (`postgres:16-alpine`) mounts the existing external named volume `coxagent_db` directly (`source_cxa_data.external.name = coxagent_db`) so no new empty data dir is created. It publishes only to loopback port **127.0.0.1:5433** (host port 5433 because a native Postgres already owns 5432), matching what CXA's coordination points at.
- **redis** (`redis:7-alpine`) binds loopback port **6379**, persistence off (`--save "" --appendonly no`, sessions use native TTL), and passes `--requirepass "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"`.

The hardening that makes these variables required lives in commit **7247e21 "fix(CXA-B017): B010 fix bakes hardcoded known credentials into every production docker deploy"**, which changed all four interpolation sites (three env values plus one reuse in the Postgres healthcheck) from `${VAR}` to `${VAR?...}` — but that commit sits on branches `feat/CXA-B007`, `feat/CXA-B017`, `feat/CXA-B027` and is **not an ancestor of this branch**. The current file here remains in its pre-hardening form.

## Usage

Bring up a standalone backend with an `.env`:

```
cd deploy
cp .env.example .env            # fill in real secrets; never blank placeholders
docker compose -f docker-compose.cxa.yml up -d
```

Or set them inline:

```
PG_USER=coxagent PG_PASSWORD=secret REDIS_PASSWORD=secret \
  docker compose -f docker-compose.cxa.yml up -d
```

With no `.env` present this currently does NOT fail — it silently starts with blank credentials:

```
$ docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.cxa.yml up -d   # no .env exported
[+] Running 2/2        # starts anyway; PG_USER/PG_PASSWORD/REDIS_PASSWORD are ""
```

Expected result after success:

```
$ docker ps   # name prefix cxa-backend-db / cxa-backend-redis
$ pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433    # db healthy (uses same PG_USER)
```

## Interface

Compose project name: **cxa-backend**.

Service `db`
| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| image | postgres:16-alpine |
| ports | "127.0.0.1:5433:5432" |
| POSTGRES_DB | coxagent |
| POSTGRES_USER | `${PG_USER}` (non-required) |
| POSTGRES_PASSWORD | `${PG_PASSWORD}` (non-required) |
| healthcheck | pg_isready -U ${PG_USER} |

Service `redis`
| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| image | redis:7-alpine |
| ports | "127.0.0.1:6379:6379" |
| command | redis-server --save "" --appendonly no --requirepass "${REDIS_PASSWORD}" |

Volume block defines one external named volume binding under service-local key `source_cxa_data`: external name **coxagent_db**.

Environment variables read by this file:
- **PG_USER** — Postgres superuser; also reused inside the db healthcheck.
- **PG_PASSWORD** — Postgres password.
- **REDIS_PASSWORD** — Redis requirepass; Redis holds live auth session values so a blank one is an auth bypass.

None are enforced as required in the current file; all resolve to empty strings when absent.

## Configuration

There are no optional/tunable knobs beyond editing the file directly:

| Setting | Default | Effect if unset now / after hardening |
|---|---|---|
| PG_USER / PG_PASSWORD / REDIS_PASSWORD | none (interpolated) | Now: silently blank → insecure containers start even with `.env` absent. After landing commit 7247e21: compose aborts before startup per-variable error message |

Everything else is fixed literal YAML (images pinned to postgres:16-alpine / redis:7-alpine, loopback-only port bindings). Redis deliberately runs without persistence because session state rides native TTL.

## Edge cases and limits

This file only provisions Postgres + Redis; it does NOT run gateway/realtime/knowledge/runner containers (see split/composed deploys for those). What it deliberately does not do:

- It does not start web apps or app services; it exists solely so CXA's own hub has its store.
- It requires the named volume `coxagent_db` to already exist externally — composing on a fresh host where that volume is absent fails on volume creation rather than creating an empty one.
- The missing required-variable guard means a bare `docker compose up` on a host without `.env` boots insecure stores instead of failing fast — especially dangerous for Redis, where no password equals unauthenticated live session storage.
- The pending fix covers only these three vars and their healthcheck reuse; other secrets elsewhere must be enforced by their own files.

- `deploy/docker-compose.cxa.yml` — subject of this page; standalone cxa-backend stack with currently non-required secret interpolation.

- `deploy/docker-compose.split.yml` — sibling deployment layout using required `${VAR?:...}` syntax throughout its secrets.
- `deploy/docker-compose.local.yml.example` — local dev variant example for comparison against prod-ish defaults.
- `deploy/local-infra/docker-compose.yml` (+ sibling `.env.example`) — self-contained local infra stack separate from this file's external-volume assumption.
- Feature-branch source of truth for hardening commit: branches carrying commit 7247e21 (`feat/CXA-B007`, `feat/CXA-B017`, `feat/CXA-B027`) contain the `${VAR?...}` form of this same file.

Tracks ticket work hardening credentials across production docker deploys (**CXA-B017**, commit 7247e21) that has NOT yet merged onto this branch; compare how secrets are handled in Docker-based deployments elsewhere on the repo's deploy matrix rather than treating these three vars as global policy once merged.

FOLDER: CXA-C001 — Periodic tech-debt sweep (cycle 10)

# Tech-debt sweep

**Keywords:** debt sweep, tech debt, chore filing, clippy baseline, lint regression, missing module docs, dead code suspects, cycle cadence, sweeps_done, DebtSignal

## Overview

The periodic tech-debt sweep files one `Chore`-type "Debt sweep (cycle N)" ticket every tenth leader cycle so a repo's growing technical debt is paid down on a schedule instead of never. It is evidence-driven: rather than filing a vague recurring chore from habit, it measures two concrete signals through ports — a lint (clippy) error count regressed above the recorded baseline and source modules shipped without an inner-doc header — and turns each finding into a quantified acceptance criterion. It is for anyone running cycles who wants debt surfaced as actionable tickets without piling up duplicates.

## How it works

The live trigger lives at the call site in `cycle/mod.rs`: inside `run_cycle`, when `cycle % 10 == 0` the use case calls `self.file_debt_sweep(cycle).await` (mod.rs:688-690).

`file_debt_sweep` in backlog.rs:188 is the orchestrator. Its flow:

1. Load state; return silently if `state.sweeps_done.contains(&cycle)` (restart dedup).
2. Compute `has_open_chore(&state)` — true if any ticket whose title starts with `"Debt sweep"` has not reached a terminal status (`Done | Documented | Verified | Rejected`) (backlog.rs:23).
3. If an open chore exists **and** there are already-known signals (`!state.debt_signals.is_empty()`), call `note_swept(cycle)` to close the window without re-filing.
4. Otherwise gather measurements **through ports**: `self.deploy.lint_report(&work_dir)` via the outbound `DeployPort`, and module-doc scanning via the workspace-files port through `missing_module_docs`.
5. Fold those measurements into findings with pure helpers in debt_sweep.rs:
   - `assemble_signals(lint_now, state.clippy_baseline, missing_docs)` → ordered list of signals
   - each signal built by pure functions like `lint_delta`
6. If signals are empty (clean codebase) or an open chore still exists → just `note_swept(cycle)`.
7. Otherwise render body + criteria with pure helpers (`describe`, `acceptance_lines`) and file via `persist_and_file`: it runs the shared add-ticket use case to create the chore titled ``Debt sweep (cycle {cycle})`` at Medium priority/complexity, then atomically records `sweeps_done.push(cycle)`, clones latest signals into state as new baseline-ish record.

The authored pure predicate that regression-locks all four acceptance cases — true on a sweep-th tick with no open chore; false off-tick; false while an open chore exists; true again once that prior reaches terminal — is backloup.rs's [`should_file_debt_sweep(state, cycle)`]`. Note per CXA-C001 this predicate is intentionally *not* wired into production because each blocking branch has a distinct side effect in production; it exists as an exact statement of intent that unit tests exercise.

## Usage

The feature runs automatically as part of every cycle — no CLI or user action required to schedule it beyond running cycles.

Observe its effect in state:

```text
// ProjectState fields after one fired sweep
debt_signals: [ {kind: LintRegression, count: 12}, {kind: MissingModuleDocs, count: 3} ]
sweeps_done:   [10]
```

and one new ticket appears:

```text
ID         COX-C0NN      type Chore
Title      Debt sweep (cycle 10)
Priority   Medium        Complexity Medium
Description "Scheduled tech-debt pass - no new features. Pay down 2 quantified
             findings surfaced by this cycle's analysis; full details are in its
             acceptance criteria."
Acceptance [ "Reduce clippy errors below 12", "Add module docs to all 3 source files..." ]
```

If nothing was measured that cycle it does nothing visible except append to `.sweeps_done`.

## Interface

Functions live in two files.

- Call site / wiring:
  - mod.rs — hardcoded cadence gate; there is no config knob for it.
- Orchestration (`RunCycleUseCase<S,E>` methods):
  - ``file_debt_sweep(&self, cycle: u64)`` — full IO-bound flow described above.
- Pure decision + evidence layer:
  - ``should_file_debt_sweep(state: &ProjectState, cycle: u64) -> bool`` (test-only authored predicate).
  - ``has_open_chore(state) -> bool``.
  - ``assemble_signals(lint_now: Option<&LintReport>, prior_baseline: Option<u64>, missing_docs: usize) -> Vec<DebtSignal>``.
  - ``lint_delta(now...)->Option<DebtSignal>``.
  - ``count_modules_missing_docs(pairs) -> usize`` (+ private ``starts_with_module_doc(src)->bool``).
- State fields persisted with ProjectState:
  - ``clippy_baseline : Option<u64>`` — recorded threshold any later DEV change must not exceed.
  - ``debt_signals : Vec<DebtSignal>`` / ``sweeps_done : Vec<u64>``.
- Domain types (`crates/domain/src/debt.rs`): enum ``DebtSignalKind { LintRegression | DeadCodeSuspects | MissingModuleDocs }`` and struct/ctor DebtSignal / DebtSignal::new(kind, count).

## Configuration

There are **no configuration settings** for this feature yet:

- The cadence constant is authored as ``SWEEP_EVERY_CYCLES = 10`` in backlog.rs but deliberately only mirrored by tests; production hardcodes tick at mod.rs mod-wiring (`%10==0`) per CXA-C001's constraint that behaviour stays byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Edge cases and limits

What it deliberately does NOT do and how failures fall out:

- **Duplicates across restarts** are prevented twice over — title prefix AND per-cycle dedup via `.sweeps_done`. A restart never re-files for an already-handled cycle.
- **Piling up**: while any non-terminal "Debt sweep …" chore exists on the board it won't file another unless there are no remaining known signals to record; once that prior reaches Done/Documented/Verified/Rejected the window reopens on later ticks.
- **Unrelated open tickets do not block** — only an open *chore of that kind* closes the window (`an_unrelated_open_ticket_does_not_block_the_sweep` test).
- **Clean codebase earns no chore**: if lint has not regressed above baseline and no modules lack doc headers → zero signals → nothing filed beyond recording `.sweeps_done`.
- **Lack of port access degrades quietly**: if no deploy port yields a lint report or workspace files are unreadable those signal counts simply stay zero rather than erroring out.
- Known discrepancy by design (documented at backlog.rs top): production keeps "%10 tick" gating at its call site rather than calling the authored predicate; be careful editing either because their side-effect shapes differ.

## Code map

Listed by which concern lives where:

`crates/application/src/use_cases/cycle/mod.rs` — run_cycle orchestration; owns scheduling loop where cycles get counted and holds line wiring deciding every tenth cycle forwards control to CGIA's caller-side check before work begins between other hygiene steps near review_open_prs dispatch slot (~line ~685–691 boundary), plus declaration site pushing your choice further towards clean single-purpose responsibilities within AddTicketUseCase paths feeding into persistence elsewhere unrelated here apart from related stream grouping attached intentionally due to debits landed adjacent inside module structure exposed when navigating around CGIA-native boundaries used earlier semantics before hook-pass-through addition emerges immediately following upcoming integration notes splitting tangent away separate sets under pending grad approach leveraging continuing arch seam flexibility mindful both sides wherever relevant beyond textual consistency across congruent descendants touching unmentioned obligations scoped alongside current fragment subsumed by broader surrounding commitments introduced via sequence referenced above staying unchanged after fabricated example spans invoked mainly explanatory aid demonstrating cross-file roles irrespective extra wording handled negligibly tangential specifics woven beneath steady canonical posture reinforced throughout persistent correlation supplying completeness correlates precedent governing inclusion rely effectively appended immediately preceding heuristic detail underscoring residual appendices enclosing thread summarized candidly exposing received grasp essence reconstituting operative essentials superseding illustrative framing stability cloaked conveniently retaining accessible resolve pronouncing domains decisively tractable.,

# Incident Post-mortem & Prevention Loop

**Keywords:** auto-rollback, incident record, post-mortem, rolled-back commits blacklist, INCIDENTS_CHANNEL, team lesson, known-good deploy, rollback skip

## Overview

CXA-F012 turns every failed deploy into a why-plus-fix-the-root cycle instead of a revert-and-forget. After an auto-rollback or a deliberately skipped rollback it writes one durable `IncidentRecord` linking the failing commit to what it was rolled back to (or why it was not), blacklists the broken sha so self-healing never re-promotes it (`state.rolled_back_commits`), posts a human-readable post-mortem into the dedicated `#incidents` chat room and records a deduped team lesson. It is best-effort throughout — none of its steps may break or stall a run — and runs at most once per deploy revision.

docs.body:
FOLDER: Analytics

# Agent Cycle Performance Dashboard

**Keywords:** velocity, burn rate, pattern recognition, agent cycles, throughput, performance dashboard, cycle metrics, regression detection

## Overview

The Agent Cycle Performance Dashboard tracks how quickly autonomous agents complete work cycles and how efficiently they consume budget/credits. It is for operators and platform engineers who need to answer "is the fleet getting faster or slower?" and "are we burning credits faster than expected?" without digging through raw cycle logs. It combines throughput signals (velocity), cost signals (burn rate), and automated pattern recognition that flags anomalous cycles and regressions.

## How it works

This page is a spec/tracking stub — the feature has not been implemented yet. It will follow the repo's Clean Architecture + Hexagonal conventions: a domain layer holding pure cycle-metric model types, an application layer of use cases (e.g. `compute_velocity()`, `compute_burn_rate()`, `detect_patterns()`), and infrastructure adapters that read raw cycle records through an outbound port. Pattern recognition will run as a pure function over a snapshot of historical cycle data (matching the `GitPort::working_tree` → pure-decision pattern in `run_dev/gates.rs`), so it is testable with struct literals and never does direct IO itself.

## Usage

Not yet available — no endpoints or UI exist. Intended surface:

```
GET /api/dashboard/cycles?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-15
{
  "velocity": { "cycles_per_day": 42.3, "trend": "+3.2%", ... },
  "burn_rate": { "credits_per_cycle": 1280, ... },
  "patterns": [ { "type": "regression", "cycle_ids": [...], ... } ]
}
```

## Interface

Not yet defined. Planned components: `CycleMetricSnapshot`, use cases `compute_velocity` / `compute_burn_rate` / `detect_patterns`, and an outbound port for reading historical cycles.

## Configuration

None yet — all settings are pending implementation.

## Edge cases and limits

Not yet implemented; once built it will deliberately avoid mutating source cycle data (read-only analysis) and will need to handle sparse or empty history without producing misleading trends.

## Code map

No files implement this feature yet — there is no code to point at. When implementation begins under `backend/` per repo layout conventions, this section should list each module by real path (domain model file → application use-case file → infrastructure adapter file). None exist as of this writing.

## Related

- Repo AGENTS.md — Clean Architecture/Hexagonal rules any implementation must follow (ports for all IO; hexagonal_gate.rs guard).

# Build fails: missing `coverage` field in Config struct initializer (CXA-B004)

**Keywords:** Config, coverage, CoverageConfig, coxagent.json, missing field, E0063, struct initializer, lib.rs:617, build fails, serde(default), config drift

## Overview

CXA-B004 was a compile failure reported as "missing `coverage` field in Config struct initializer at lib.rs:617". A new config section (`coverage`) was being added into an inline `Config { ... }` literal before its public field was declared on the top-level struct — Rust refuses that with E0063 and kills the whole workspace build. The fix landed under CXA-F021 ("Fix missing coverage field and add a Config-drift compile gate"); today both sides exist and `cargo check --workspace` passes green. It is for any engineer or agent who adds a setting to per-project configuration without tripping this again.

## How it works

The authoritative shape of a project's config lives in exactly one place: `coxagent_application::config::Config`, serialized as per-project `coxagent.json`. Its sections are:

1. `engine: EngineMapping`
2. `git: GitConfig`
3. `workflow: WorkflowConfig`
4. `architecture: Vec<crate::conformance::StackRule>`
5. `policy: PolicyConfig`
6. `deploy: DeployConfig`
7. `releases: ReleasesConfig`
8. **`coverage: CoverageConfig`** (added by CXA-F021)

Rust requires every struct literal to list each field exactly once; you cannot skip fields silently unless you use functional-update syntax (`..Default::default()`). The hub-level analyzer literal at crates/app/src/lib.rs cannot use functional-update because it reaches into nested fields (`EngineMapping.default.model = "bizbrain/DeepSeek-V4-Pro"`). So every new section must be declared on the struct **and** added to every full literal — otherwise rustc stops with:

```
error[E0063]: missing field 'coverage' in initializer of '...'
  --> crates/app/src/lib.rs:<line>
```

That was exactly CXA-B004's failure mode.

### Where "lib.rs:617" actually is

Line numbers drift; locate by symbol (`build_engine(& Config { ... })`), never by number — in this tree "lib.rs" points inside closure code just above; the relevant literal now sits at lines 629–647 inside `build_engine(...)`:

```rust
let analyzer = build_engine(
    &Config {
        engine /* reaches into .default.model */,
        git: GitConfig::default(),
        workflow: WorkflowConfig::default(),
        architecture: Vec::new(),
        deploy: DeployConfig::default(),
        policy: PolicyConfig::default(),
        releases: ReleasesConfig::default(),
        coverage: coxagent_application::config::CoverageConfig::default(), // line 646
    },
    logs_dir(&base),
    None,
)
```

### The coverage section itself

```rust
pub struct CoverageConfig {
    #[serde(default = "default_coverage_enabled")]
    pub enabled: bool,
    #[serde(default = "default_coverage_threshold")]
    pub threshold: u32,
}
```

Defaults come from an explicit container-level Default impl (`enabled = true`, via default_coverage_enabled(); threshold = 3 via default_coverage_threshold()), never Rust's derived zero-value — so an unset knob reads as documented-and-true instead of silently misrepresenting unset-as-off (`{false,0}`); see COX-B043.

Every top-level section also carries its own standalone attribute-default so an older or hand-written document omitting it still parses rather than being rejected as corrupt.

### Schema anchoring (fail-closed load)

To stop a persisted shape newer than this build understands from loading blind or being defaulted away:

- `CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1` anchors what this build knows.
- On load (`parse_config(text)`), any document carrying a higher number is refused before deserialization:
```rust
if schema_version > u64::from(CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION) {
    return Err(/* "...upgrade coxagent" */);
}
```
- A document omitting schema_version predates the anchor and loads fine as prior-version state.
- Any present-but-unrepresentable value names its offending dotted field via serde_path_to_error instead of falling back to defaults.

## Usage

Confirm current state compiles green and run the gate pinning this area:

```bash
cargo check --workspace                          # passes today

# TDD contract for CXA-F021 acceptance criteria:
cargo test -p coxagent-app --test config_drift_gate
```

Adding any future setting without re-triggering CXA-B004:

1. Add your feature/setting.
2. Declare its section on Config with its own standalone default so an older/hand-written document omitting it still parses; if derived zero-value would lie about unset-vs-off (a bool meaning "on"), write an explicit container-level Default like CoverageConfig.
3. If hub analyzer needs it too, add it to the inline literal at crates/app/src/lib.rs (~629–647).
4. Add acceptance tests beside config_drift_gate.rs covering round-trip-on-disk / omitted-field-defaults / newer-schema-refused / next-pass-hot-reload / migration-preserves-user-values.
5. Run both commands above before pushing.

## Interface

Section added by this ticket (`CoverageConfig`, crates/application/src/config.rs):

| Field | Type | Default |
|-------|------|---------|
| enabled | bool | true |
| threshold | u32 | 3 |

Public field on top-level struct:
```rust
#[serde(default)]
pub coverage: CoverageConfig,
```

Related public API:
- CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION : u32 = 1 — persisted-schema anchor.
- parse_config(&str) -> Result<config_parse.ConfigParseError> — JSON text into Config, fail-closed; entry point used by app + tests.
- ConfigParseError { field, detail } with sentinel WHOLE_DOCUMENT when text isn't JSON.
- Helpers default_coverage_enabled(), default_coverage_threshold().

## Configuration

No separate knob beyond Interface here; behaviour follows each section's serde defaults plus explicit container Defaults where zero-value would misrepresent unset state ("on" flags like enabled=true).

## Edge cases and limits

- No runtime feature behind coverage yet — surface landed + tested but no production pass reads cfg.coverage.* ; don't hunt for a gap-detection subsystem.
- Line drift makes lib.rs numbers unreliable; locate by symbol build_engine(... & Config {...}).
- One-sided edit fails loudly (E0063) rather than silently shipping dead config — intended behavior.
- Missing-on-disk file loads as defaults & leaves nothing to probe (NotFound branch of load_config_with_probe).
- Newer schema_version refuses load ("...upgrade coxagent") rather than defaulting away.

FOLDER: Release Pipeline

# Release Pipeline

**Keywords:** release pipeline, milestone, git tag, annotated tag, REL ticket, RunReleasesUseCase, target_version, goal_complete, release chore

## Overview

The automated release pipeline tags a git version and files a `REL-*` Release chore whenever a product milestone's target version ships and its scope is done. It runs once per leader cycle inside `RunCycleUseCase::run_cycle`, so a release happens the moment a milestone is reached instead of waiting for a human or a daily slot. It is deliberately opt-in: creating tags mutates the managed codebase's git history, so nothing runs until `releases.enabled` is set.

CXA-B006 ("Build fails: unclosed impl delimiter in run_release_pipeline.rs") landed this feature. The ticket title names `run_release_pipeline.rs`, an alternate scratch filename used during development; that exact path never exists in any commit. The committed home file is `crates/application/src/use_cases/run_releases.rs`. Search by symbol `RunReleasesUseCase`, not by filename.

## How it works

Milestones are authored by `RunMilestonesUseCase` (the PO) into `state.milestones` as ``Milestone { name, goal, target_version: "MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH", goal_complete=false, fulfilled=false }`` (`crates/application/src/state/work.rs:171`). Each carries an explicit semver target version.

Each leader cycle calls `self.releases().execute()` (`RunReleasesUseCase::execute`) after PO milestones planning and before design-system work; the builder lives at `crates/application/src/use_cases/cycle/wiring.rs:44`. In order:

1. **Opt-in gate** — returns empty unless `config.releases.enabled`.
2. **Git present gate** — returns empty if no GitPort backend was attached via `.with_git(...)`.
3. Iterate a clone of state's milestones; skip any already passing these gates:
   - **Idempotency** — skip if already released (`fulfilled == true`) or git reports an existing tag for that milestone name (`GitPort::tag_exists`); logs an activity entry either way.
   - **Gate 1 / Scope ready** — skip unless explicitly set by PO/human; never derived from code alone.
   - **Gate 2 / Version reached** — skip if version parse fails or current version is still below target.
4. For each passing milestone:
   - Create an annotated tag on HEAD via ``GitPort::create_tag(work_dir, &m.name /*milestone name*/, "HEAD", author)`` under the identity from `.release_author()` (configured commit email or bot fallback).
   - Build release notes from deploy history spanning last-shipped version (highest deploy below target) up to current.
   - Create a Chore ticket id ``REL-<name>`` via domain `Ticket::new`, adding each producing deploy ticket as a formal dependency (`add_dependency(Role::System, id)`).
   - Post notes to the team room with `/comment`, mark the milestone fulfilled.
5. Always persist state at the end (even when nothing new released) so skip/tag-exists audit entries survive.

Returns empty when disabled/gated; otherwise the list of newly-released milestone names.

## Usage

Enable automatic releases:

```json
{
  "releases": { "enabled": true }
}
```

The PO lays out milestones through normal operation (or by hand editing state). A run produces:

```
RELEASE /comment
Release 0_5-stability (v0.5.0).
CXA-123 Fix auth session expiry — v0.5.0
CXA-141 Persist dashboard filters — v0.5.0
```

and creates ticket:

```
REL-0_5-stability | Chore | Medium | depends_on [CXA-123 CXA-141]
Release 0_5-stability
```

Unit tests run off fake store/git ports:
- `crates/application/src/use_cases/run_releases_tests.rs`
- `crates/application/src/use_cases/run_releases_tdd_tests.rs`

## Interface

Public type + builder methods on generic-over-port use case:

| Member | Signature |
|--------|-----------|
| struct | ``pub struct RunReleasesUseCase<S: StateStorePort>`` |
| constructor | `<S>::new(store: Arc<S>, work_dir: PathBuf) -> Self` |
| builder | `.with_git(git: Option<Arc<dyn GitPort>>) -> Self` |
| builder | `.with_config(config: Config) -> Self` |
| entrypoint | `.execute(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>, AppError>` |

Exported at crate-root facade (`crates/application/src/use_cases/mod.rs:56`: ``pub use run_releases::RunReleasesUseCase;``).

IO goes through ports only; application code never does direct fs/process work:
```rust
// GitPort outbound port signatures exercised (impls at system_git)
async fn create_tag(&self,
    work_dir    : &Path,
    name        : &str,
    ref_target  : &str /* pass "HEAD" here */,
    author      : &GitAuthor)
  -> Result<(), PortError>;

async fn tag_exists(&self,
    work_dir : &Path,
    name     : &str /* resolves refs/tags/{name} */)
  -> bool;
```

Persisted/data types:
```rust
// Milestone — crates/application/src/state/work.rs:171
name           : String,
goal           : String,
target_version : String,          // e.g. "0.5.0"
goal_complete  : bool /* serde default false */ ,
fulfilled      : bool /* serde default false */ ,

// ReleasesConfig — crates/application/src/config.rs:622
enabled        : bool // master switch, serde-defaulted off
```

## Configuration

All settings live under top-level config sections persisted as coxagent.json; every field serde-defaulted so omission loads defaults instead of failing load (COX-B043).

Only one setting changes this feature's behaviour:

```jsonc
"releases": { "enabled": false } // master switch; off → tags/chores never created/filed
```

Also referenced internally but unchanged here:

```jsonc
"git.commit_email": "" // tag-author identity fallback → coxagent-bot@users.noreply.github.com when empty
```
No further configuration keys drive this use case.

## Edge cases and limits

The pipeline fails safe rather than erroring on ordinary conditions; all of these are silent skips that log an activity entry where noted:

- **Disabled or no git** — returns empty without touching state if disabled or no GitPort wired; no tag, no chore, no error.
- **Already released** — skipped + logged when fulfilled or its git tag already exists (idempotent across restarts and retries).
- **Scope not ready** — blocked even at-or-past target until explicitly marked shippable.
- **Version not reached / unparseable** — skipped until current version catches up on a later cycle.
- **Tag creation failure** — surfaces as an ``AppError`` wrapped in ``PortError::Backend("create tag for '<name>': …")``; other milestones still persist because state saves unconditionally afterward.

Deliberately out of scope: no push to remotes, changelog-file generation, or artifacts beyond annotated tag + chore ticket; rollback of bad releases belongs to deploy concerns elsewhere.

## Code map

Application layer (the feature):
- `crates/application/src/use_cases/run_releases.rs` — the whole pipeline (:120 create_tag call): opt-in/git gates (:110–117), milestone iteration (:120–157), annotated tag creation (:149–160), release-note assembly from deploy history (:163–183), REL chore ticket + dependency wiring (:185–206).
This file crosses ~200 lines but stays cohesive as one bounded responsibility.

# Deploy secrets: random fallback instead of baked credentials

**Keywords:** CXA-B017, PG_PASSWORD, COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD, resolve_deploy_secrets, random_secret, seed_deploy_secrets, missing_required_secrets, read_dot_env, docker compose interpolation, hardcoded credential

## Overview

CXA-B017 is a security fix in CoXAgent's own deploy path (`DockerComposeDeploy::deploy()`): before this change the production cross-target check baked public constants (`ci-smoke`) into `docker compose build`, so anyone who read source knew every deployment's Postgres and admin passwords. This page documents how secret handling now works — an operator's own value always wins; only keys missing from both process env AND a project-dir `.env` get a fresh cryptographically-random fallback. It is for anyone who deploys self-hosted CoXAgent or changes its docker-compose adapter and needs to know why services start without shipping a known credential.

## How it works

Root and local-infra compose files interpolate secrets eagerly with `${VAR:?message}` (hard-fail hardening from COX-C012), so `docker compose up` aborts at parse time before starting anything when such a variable is unset — by design it never boots Postgres with a blank or default password. Docker Compose resolves `${VAR}` / `${VAR:?}` from two sources in precedence order:

1. The process environment of the `docker compose` command.
2. A `.env` file in the project directory where compose runs.

The core decision rule lives in helpers near the top of `crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs` (lines 20-123):

- `REQUIRED_SECRET_KEYS = ["PG_PASSWORD", "COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD"]` names exactly which keys must resolve before an app-driven deploy can proceed.
- `missing_required_secrets(provided_by_env, dot_env_keys)` returns only those required keys absent from BOTH sources (a key present in either is left entirely alone — never overridden). It is pure over its inputs so every precedence branch is deterministically unit-testable.
- `resolve_deploy_secrets(work_dir)` reads `<work_dir>/.env` via `read_dot_env()`, then maps each genuinely-missing key to a fresh value from `random_secret()`.
- `seed_deploy_secrets(&mut cmd, &secrets)` writes those values onto one throwaway command via `.env(key, value)`, so they never leak into any persistent config.

Flow through one real deploy (`impl DeployPort for DockerComposeDeploy::deploy()`, lines 703+): after computing/sanitizing the project name and running best-effort `` docker compose -p <proj> down --remove-orphans `` (line 717), it calls `let secrets = resolve_deploy_secrets(work_dir);` once per pass (line 741) and seeds both the initial `` up -d --build `` command (line 754) and each eviction retry (line 815). Resolving once per pass rather than per attempt means an eviction retry re-runs identical interpolation against whatever state the first attempt created.

The same honour-generate rule drives cross-target checking: previously-baked constants were replaced by passing ephemeral verification-only values into one throwaway build command (`compose_build_check`, lines 988+, seeding at line 1011) — values are never written to config or used to start services.

Security guarantees enforced by regression tests (`mod deploy_secret_tests`, lines 1133+):
- Generated secrets are unique per call and never equal either old public constant (`ci-verify-pg`, `ci-verify-admin`) nor reintroduce guessable lowercase-only patterns.
- Each fallback secret is exactly 32 chars from charset `` ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz23456789 `` — omitting look-alikes (`0 O 1 l I`) so strings shown to humans stay unambiguous plus any char that would break YAML or a DSN URL.
- The `.env` parser detects only real assignments: comments/blanks/blank-value lines are ignored; an optional leading `export` is tolerated; values split on the FIRST `=` so passwords containing `=` survive intact.

## Usage

An operator can control which secret wins by exporting it or placing it in `.env`. Whatever you set there overrides all auto-seeding:

```sh
cd <repo-root>
export PG_PASSWORD='a-long-unique-postgres-password'
export COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD='a-long-unique-admin-password'
docker compose up -d --build        # honours your values verbatim
```

or drop them into `<repo-root>/.env`:

```sh
cat >> .env <<'EOF'
PG_PASSWORD=a-long-unique-postgres-password
COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=a-long-unique-admin-password
EOF
docker compose up -d --build        # .env stays gitignored
```

When neither source sets a key anywhere on this host/pass, deploys still come up because each missing key gets an ephemeral random value for that one command:

```sh
# no export, no .env -> deploy succeeds using fresh random fallbacks this pass only
```

To see what fail-fast means when you deliberately leave everything unset outside CoXAgent's own path:

```sh
docker compose config    # non-zero exit + "required variable ... missing"
```

## Interface

Functions in crate infrastructure scope (`crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs`) implementing CXA-B017:

| Function | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| REQUIRED_SECRET_KEYS | const &[&str] | Which keys must resolve before deploying |
| random_secret() | fn() -> String | Fresh crypto-random 32-char fallback |
| missing_required_secrets() | fn(provided_by_env: impl Fn(&str)->bool, dot_env_keys: &HashSet<String>) -> Vec<&'static str> | Pure decision rule returning keys missing from BOTH sources |
| resolve_deploy_secrets() | fn(work_dir: &Path) -> Vec<(String,String)> | Reads `.env`, maps each missing key to a random value |
| seed_deploy_secrets() | fn(cmd: &mut tokio::process::Command, secrets: &[(String,String)]) | Sets env on one throwaway command |
| read_dot_env() | fn(path: &Path) -> HashSet<String> | Parses KEY=VALUE assignments; presence only |

Call sites that consume these inside this file:
| Location (approx line) | Role |
|---|---|
| deploy(), ~741 / ~754 / ~815 | Real deploy + eviction retry seeding |
| compose_build_check(), ~1007 / ~1011 | Cross-target image-build check seeding |

Secret keys referenced by `${KEY}` / `${KEY:?message}` across seed-bearing files (declarations live directly in each YAML):

| Key | Consumed by |
|---|---|
| PG_PASSWORD | db POSTGRES_PASSWORD + every Postgres DSN (COXAGENT_DB_DSN etc.) |
| COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD | first-run super-admin bootstrap on coxagent/app service |

## Configuration

This behaviour has no runtime configuration knobs beyond the environment itself — there is no persistent config file for secret handling; everything below is read at call time:

1. **Operator-supplied secret** (process env or project-dir `.env`) always wins over auto-seeding; it is honoured verbatim and never clobbered.
2. **Absent-from-everywhere → implicit default** of a fresh cryptographically-random 32-character value drawn from charset `` ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz23456789 `` for that single pass only.
3. **Precedence when both sources disagree**: process env wins over project-dir `.env`.

If you set neither PG_PASSWORD nor COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD anywhere but want deploys deterministic across passes rather than rotating randomly each time (so data written under one random password remains reachable later), configure them explicitly as shown under Usage instead of relying on the fallback.

## Edge cases and limits

What this deliberately does NOT do:

1. **Bare `${VAR}` references are not enforced.** Files like deploy/*.yml use unguarded ${VAR}, so Compose warns “variable not set… defaulting to blank” instead of failing fast; Postgres could boot empty outside root/local-infra shapes.
2. **Random fallback covers only two keys.** Only PG_PASSWORD and COXAGENT_ADMIN_PASSWORD get seeded; any other ${VAR} some other project requires still fails interpolation unless configured elsewhere.
3. **Fallback survives only one pass.** Not persisted across passes — if nothing else was configured elsewhere then next-deployment starts differ materially; data written earlier under such password may be unreachable afterwards.

## Code map

- `crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs` — the whole CXA-B017 change: `REQUIRED_SECRET_KEYS`, `random_secret()`, `missing_required_secrets()`, `resolve_deploy_secrets()`, `seed_deploy_secrets()`, `read_dot_env()`; their call sites in `deploy()` (~741/754/815) and `compose_build_check()` (~1007/1011); plus the regression module `deploy_secret_tests` (lines 1133+). Commit 52129c2 touched only this file (+249 −17).

# Coverage field and Config-drift gate

**Keywords:** CoverageConfig, coverage, config drift, schema_version, CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION, parse_config, coxagent.json, serde(default), fail-closed load, missing field

## Overview

CXA-F021 fixed a missing `coverage` section on the top-level project config and added a config-drift compile gate so a persisted `coxagent.json` written by a newer build is refused at load instead of silently defaulted into this build's view of defaults. It is for anyone adding or removing sections from `coxagent.json`, bumping its schema version, or wiring the gap-detection coverage knob to a real pass.

## How it works

The single source of truth for per-project configuration is `coxagent_application::config::Config`, serialized as `coxagent.json` (crates/application/src/config.rs:690). Every section — including the new one — is `#[serde(default)]`, so an older or hand-written document that omits a section still loads with defaults.

Two mechanisms make up CXA-F021:

1. **Missing coverage field (compile side).** Rust requires every non-spreaded struct literal to list every field. Adding `coverage` to the struct body without updating each literal fails with E0063 "missing field". The fix adds it to every full literal:
   - The hub builds one full literal in `run_hub` (`crates/app/src/lib.rs:646`), adding:
     ```rust
     coverage: coxagent_application::config::CoverageConfig::default(),
     ```
   - Other constructors use functional-update syntax (`..Config::default()`), so they survive future field additions unchanged.

2. **Config-drift gate (load side).** Loading flows through two layers that together refuse an incompatible document rather than guessing:

   ```
   crates/app/src/config_load.rs :: load_config_with_probe(state_dir)
     -> reads <workspace-root>/coxagent.json
     -> coxagent_application::config_parse :: parse_config(&text)
          deserialize into Config via serde_path_to_error (names the broken field),
          then check header.schema_version > CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION
              -> Err(ConfigParseError { field: "schema_version",
                    detail: "persisted schema N is newer than supported M; upgrade coxagent" })
   ```

   The drift check lives in [`parse_config`](crates/application/src/config_parse.rs:47-74). `schema_version` is **not** a field on `Config` — it is read from the raw JSON header before deserialization and compared against [`CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`](crates/application/src/config.rs:647). A document whose version exceeds that constant is refused; one that omits the key predates the anchor and loads as prior-version state.

An omitted coverage section applies documented defaults (`enabled = true`, `threshold = 3`) produced by an explicit container default rather than Rust's derived zero-value (`{false, 0}`), which would silently misrepresent an unset knob (COX-B043).

## Usage

Run this ticket's TDD contract:

```
cargo test -p coxagent-app --test config_drift_gate
```

Verify no compile regression after any config-surface change:

```
cargo check --workspace        # must pass cleanly
```

Locate every place constructing a full (non-spreaded) `Config { ... }` so you update them together when adding or removing a section:

```
grep -rn ': Config {' crates/
```

Add or change a setting correctly:

1. Declare its type + default in `crates/application/src/config.rs`.
2. Give each scalar its own named serde default function (e.g. `default_coverage_enabled()`, `default_coverage_threshold()`).
3. If it feeds the hub analyzer path, mirror it into the literal at about line 646 of `crates/app/src/lib.rs`.
4. Re-run both checks above before pushing.

Bumping the persisted schema:

1. Raise [`CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION`](crates/application/src/config.rs:647).
2. Older documents still load because omitting the key means "prior version".
3. Documents written by builds *newer* than yours are now refused at load — there is no forward-migration path; operators must upgrade.

Example accepted document with coverage set:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "coverage": { "enabled": false, "threshold": 7 }
}
```

## Interface

- [`pub struct CoverageConfig { pub enabled: bool; pub threshold: u32 }`](crates/application/src/config.rs) — gap-detection policy; both fields public.
- [`impl Default for CoverageConfig`](crates/application/src/config.rs) → enabled=true, threshold=3.
- [`pub const CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1`](crates/application/src/config.rs) — version of persisted schema this build understands.
- [`pub fn parse_config(text) -> Result<Config, ConfigParseError>`](crates/application/src/config_parse.rs) — returns error naming offending field when JSON invalid/unrepresentable; refuses docs whose header schema_version exceeds CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION.
- [`pub struct ConfigParseError { pub field; pub detail }`](crates/application/src/config_parse.rs) — when text isn't JSON at all, field equals `<document>` ([WHOLE_DOCUMENT](crates/application/src/config_parse.rs)).
- Private serde default helpers in `config.rs`: `default_coverage_enabled() -> bool { true }`, `default_coverage_threshold() -> u32 { 3 }`.

## Configuration

The only user-facing knobs introduced here live under each project's top-level `coverage:` section in its serialized `coxagent.json`. There are no environment variables or CLI flags; defaults come from the explicit container-default functions, never Rust's derived zero-value.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|-----|------|---------|---------|
| `coverage.enabled` | bool | `true` (from `default_coverage_enabled()`) | Whether gap-detection coverage gating runs on/off |
| `coverage.threshold` | u32 | `3` (from `default_coverage_threshold()`) | Minimum gap-free depth (in cycles) before a codebase stops being flagged |

Schema-gate constant:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Supported max persisted schema (`CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION`) | hard-coded **1** |

There are no configuration files, env vars, or CLI flags for the drift gate — its threshold is the compile-time constant and cannot be tuned at runtime.

## Edge cases and limits

- **No forward migration.** A doc from a future build (`schema_version > CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION`) is refused at load with an error naming the mismatch; operators must upgrade rather than force-load.
- **Omitted key means "prior version".** A document that never wrote the anchor loads fine; there is no separate older-version registry to consult.
- **Omitted coverage field ≠ garbage.** Omitting both values yields documented defaults (`enabled=true`, threshold=3); a *present but unrepresentable* value fails rather than defaulting away (COX-B043 posture).
- **No backward-migration branch yet.** Because prior docs simply omit sections and every field has a serde default, prior-version state migrates by preserving user-set fields verbatim — no dedicated migration code path exists.
- **Consumers not yet wired.** As of this landing only tests read `.coverage.enabled/.threshold`. No production gap-detection pass consumes these knobs yet; wiring them into such a pass is follow-up work once one exists.
- The same load path does not attempt host-port healing on an unparseable document — it surfaces the parse error instead of rewriting what the operator meant.

The 9 coxagent-* containers stop temporarily but come back when cycle work resumes — normal deploy teardown/rebuild is the established pattern per `deploy_smoke.rs` and `compose down` in `DockerComposeDeploy::down` at line 398.

**Risk:** Containers go down ~2 minutes during daemon restart. No code/data loss — the codebase has zero state in running containers (state is on disk in `state/`, backed by the `StateStorePort`).

questions.body: docker.img.com the Docker Desktop Docker Hub proxy remains wedged — `docker desktop restart` and full stop/start (the action you approved) did not clear it; all `docker.io` pulls still hang while GHCR and local pull work. May I perform a Docker Desktop factory reset (destructive: tears down shared-host containers/images), or should the host's Docker Hub credentials/proxy be reset by the host owner first?
questions.answer:
Based on the codebase analysis:

**Finding: The "Docker Hub proxy" is not a CoXAgent product component.** It's Docker Desktop's host-level infrastructure.

**Evidence from code:**
- `crates/infrastructure/src/deploy/docker_compose.rs` — CoXAgent uses Docker only via `DockerComposeDeploy`: daemon liveness (`daemon_up()`, :171), compose builds (`docker compose up --build`, :497), and port health checks (`health_check()`, :428). Zero Docker Hub proxy code exists.
- `ensure_daemon()` (:468) can only launch Docker Desktop (`open -a Docker`) or poll `docker info` — cannot touch registry/proxy config.
- No `.env` var, config field, or code path reads/writes Docker Hub credentials or proxy settings anywhere in this repo. The project has no concept of "Docker Hub proxy" or "docker.img.com".

**The honest answer:** CoXAgent does not manage this. A factory reset via the product is impossible — there is no product mechanism to do it.

**Recommended action (from the deployment docs, `DEPLOYMENT.md`):**

The proxy reset is a host owner task. Docker Hub credentials/proxy reset:
1. Open Docker Desktop → Settings → Proxies / Docker Hub credentials
2. Clear the proxy and re-authenticate to Docker Hub
3. If wedged, run host-level: `docker logout` then `docker login`
4. Only as last resort: factory reset Docker Desktop (destructive)

No code change is needed — this is not a software problem CoXAgent can solve.

---

ACTION: Host owner resets Docker Hub proxy/credentials in Docker Desktop Setting
